Its rule: an average-loss/average-win ratio below 2x is normal for tight-stop systems, while above 5x 'the win rate is being bought on credit'.
findings.blowup_protection: Detects a hidden tail before it shows up as a blown account; the grade is independent of headline profit.
findings.evidence: Article/code snippets; numeric expectancy example.
findings.hf_relevance: Use as automated checks on every optimizer candidate from the user's TPE/walk-forward pipeline, computed per CYCLE (basket), not per position. Inference: reject if avg cycle loss / avg cycle win > about 4-5, or if bootstrapped probability of a 50% equity drawdown over 2 years exceeds a few percent.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: compute per-cycle P/L series; Wilson lower bound on cycle win rate must exceed the breakeven win rate implied by the avg loss/win ratio.

findings.mechanism: Classify regimes with Hurst, ADX and lag-1 autocorrelation, with a per-regime win-rate ledger
findings.description: RegimeRouter classifies bars using ADX (directional strength), the Hurst exponent via R/S analysis of log returns (>0.5 persistent, <0.5 anti-persistent) and lag-1 autocorrelation (does a move follow through or snap back). It routes trend bars to breakout logic and range bars to z-score mean reversion, and keeps a separate win-rate ledger per regime with a Wilson 95% lower bound. Its rationale: ADX alone measures directional strength but says nothing about whether returns are persistent or mean-reverting. There is also an MQL5 series article on Hurst estimators for long memory.
findings.blowup_protection: Lets the grid run only in measured anti-persistent conditions, and stops it automatically when the live ledger for that regime shows a lower bound below breakeven.
findings.evidence: Code Base snippets.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: the most direct grid-friendliness measure for a 1-30 min M1 grid is negative lag-1 autocorrelation (or Hurst < 0.5) of 1-min returns over the last 1-3 hours, combined with low ADX on M5/M15. A per-regime ledger with a Wilson LB gives a self-disabling edge monitor in live trading.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: Hurst window 120-240 M1 bars; gate at H < 0.45 and ac1 < -0.05; ADX(M15) < 20-25; Wilson-LB of cycle win rate vs breakeven win rate re-evaluated weekly.

findings.mechanism: Weekend flat close with delayed, fully gated restart
findings.description: BGC forces all positions flat on Friday at a set hour and delays the restart to Monday. This covers gap risk that the continuous diffusion model behind the framework does not account for. The weekend close is treated as a cycle-ending event: the cycle counter increments, saved state is cleared, and Monday's restart passes through every normal start gate.
findings.blowup_protection: Removes weekend gap exposure and stops a stale Friday basket from carrying into a different Monday regime.
findings.evidence: Code/article snippets.
findings.hf_relevance: The user already has a Friday close. Inference: for an HF scalper also stop NEW cycles at least 30 min before the Friday flat time, so the 30-min cap and the weekend close never conflict; treat Monday's open hour as gated (gaps, wide spreads).
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: no new cycles after Friday 19:30 UTC; flat by 20:00 UTC; Monday start after spreads normalize (first 60 min blocked).

findings.mechanism: Swap avoidance: close before rollover or when swap exceeds remaining profit
findings.description: AntiSWAPcleaner estimates the applicable swap for each position and flags a position for closure when its profit is lower than the estimated swap. An MQL5 carry-trade article and a blog on overnight swap note that swap is negligible over an hour but material across several nights, and that loss limits should be measured against what the position has actually cost, including financing.
findings.blowup_protection: Stops swap from silently turning near-zero-edge baskets negative. This was one of the two costs that made every structure in our backtest negative.
findings.evidence: Product/article/blog snippets.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: with a hard 30-min cap and no cycles opened in the last 30 min before rollover, swap drops out of the P/L almost entirely. This is one of the clearest structural improvements of the HF version over v6.12.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: last new cycle = rollover - 35 min (server time, DST aware).

findings.mechanism: Cost floor: spread/commission filters that also apply to grid add orders, and ECN-only deployment
findings.description: Grid scalper listings and threads stress that micro-scalping grids are spread-sensitive and broker-dependent, and that ECN/low-spread accounts are required (spreads not above about 3 points recommended in several listings). One trader on a raw-spread account with 0.0 spread but $5.5/lot commission found the system unprofitable once fees were counted. Grid EAs expose a 'Grid Orders Comply Max Spread Condition' switch so that add orders, not just initial orders, respect the max-spread filter. Snippet attribution between the listed product/blog pages is uncertain.
findings.blowup_protection: Prevents adds during spread spikes, when fills are worst and moves are often largest. Ensures the TP actually covers round-trip costs.
findings.evidence: Search-result snippets from product pages and forum; attribution of individual sentences between the listed pages was not verifiable because the pages could not be loaded.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: let c = spread + commission per round trip in pips (about 1.2-1.5 on an Oanda-style standard account; about 0.8-0.9 on raw spread + $7/lot). Require TP >= about 4c and first spacing >= about 3c. On a standard account that forces TP >= 5-6 pips, close to v6.12's 5.3, so a 2-3 pip M1 scalping TP is structurally negative there. Apply the max-spread rule to every add, not only to cycle starts.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: max spread = 1.5 x rolling median spread for that hour; skip adds (do not queue them) while the spread is above the limit.

findings.mechanism: Capital adequacy rules of thumb and the cent-account option for $100
findings.description: Vendor minimums for grids starting at 0.01: MHV Grid $500 on one pair; Flexible Grid $1,000; GridProfit $1,000; Grid Scalper EA $4-5k per chart; Grid HLevel 0.01 per $5,000 (low risk), $2,500 (medium) or $1,000 (max profit). Forum snippets note that the 0.01 lot step is coarse for grids, and that a cent account lets a small deposit run a strategy sized like a much larger standard account.
findings.blowup_protection: Matching the lot to the capital is the first-order ruin control; finer lot granularity lets the ladder respect a % risk budget.
findings.evidence: Product page snippets (numbers above); forum snippets on cent accounts (attribution between thread pages uncertain).
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: $100 at 0.01 is 10-50x more leveraged per lot than the vendor guidance above. Either accept a very shallow ladder (about 3 flat layers) or run on a cent/micro account, where the same $100 allows a properly graded ladder (e.g. 0.1 cent-lot steps) inside a 2% budget.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: on standard, 0.01 per $100-150 equity with <= 3-4 layers per side; on cent, scale lots so each layer is about 0.02-0.03% of equity per pip.

findings.mechanism: Treat the grid account as risk capital: profit extraction, expected blow-ups, stand down on shocks
findings.description: One experienced grid trader runs 5 accounts x $1,000 with $5,000 in reserve. He starts grids only after markets stabilize and stops all systems immediately on major political, central-bank or geopolitical shocks. He expects to blow at least one account; about 6-7 of 10 accounts reach +100% in two months (about 65%). After an account doubles he withdraws 80% of profits. Another grid trader withdraws 50% of monthly profits. A grid blog recommends defined withdrawal thresholds, and a long-time BG Grid reviewer advises withdrawing profits regularly because grids eventually lose the account.
findings.blowup_protection: Caps the lifetime loss to the deposit plus un-withdrawn profits, so a single tail event cannot erase years of gains.
findings.evidence: Blog snippets with numbers above; product review snippets.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: for a $100 account, sweep profits above a ratchet (e.g. withdraw half of anything above $130) and treat the remaining balance as the option premium of the strategy.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: weekly profit sweep 50%; stop after a 25% drawdown from the account high-water mark and revalidate before redeploying.

findings.mechanism: Do not optimize the grid ladder; constrain the optimizer and validate on stress regimes
findings.description: In an MQL5 thread on optimizing grid/martingale EAs, the consensus is that optimizing the grid part makes little sense. The optimizer picks a very small gap with a bigger multiplier: baskets close faster and profits look bigger, but drawdowns and stop-outs grow on other timeframes and periods. A cross-platform grid series found that if max drawdown must stay under 20%, expected profit is unlikely to exceed 20-25% per year, and used diversification across symbols to improve the recovery factor.
findings.blowup_protection: Avoids selecting parameter sets whose apparent edge is just hidden tail exposure.
findings.evidence: Forum snippet; article snippets (20% DD -> 20-25%/yr; diversification results).
findings.hf_relevance: Directly relevant to the user's TPE/walk-forward pipeline. Inference: fix the ladder (flat), fix the risk budget, and optimize only gates (session hours, regime thresholds), spacing multiple and TP/cost multiple. Always include the 2014-15 EURUSD trend in the test set, and score by per-cycle tail metrics rather than net profit.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: objective = net profit subject to (worst cycle <= budget, avg loss/avg win <= 4, max DD <= 20%), evaluated out-of-sample per year.

findings.mechanism: Progressive (rolling) partial TP and entry pauses for abnormal conditions
findings.description: Kiwi & Roo (AUDCAD/NZDCAD M15 mean-reversion grid) layers several exposure controls. Dynamic TP, retracement close and rolling partial TP make a 'decaying grid whose exposure curve flattens instead of compounding'. Spacing is volatility-aware. Positions are closed incrementally as price starts to revert, rather than waiting for the whole basket. New entries are paused during abnormal volatility, large gaps and low-liquidity holiday periods. Vendor minimum is $1,000 per pair.
findings.blowup_protection: Shrinks basket footprint during the first part of the reversion, so a failed reversion hits a smaller basket.
findings.evidence: Vendor blog snippet (no independent numbers).
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: in a 1-30 min grid, close the newest (best-priced) layer at its own small TP as soon as price reverts one spacing. This scalps the bounce, keeps the VWAP TP for the rest, and cuts open lots before the age limit forces a market close.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: per-layer TP for the newest layer = one spacing; re-arm that layer once if price returns.

failure_modes.mode: Sustained one-way trend without a retracement (no hard basket stop)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Each new layer averages into the move, so floating loss grows quadratically with depth while margin is consumed. A single unretraced macro trend expands the basket past margin safety; 'it is not a question of if but when'. Grid/martingale systems 'do not fail slowly; they fail all at once' when margin, lot or broker limits are hit.

failure_modes.mode: Margin stop-out arrives before the 'last level' loss
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Traders budget step x N, but N legs float at step x N(N-1)/2 (10 legs = 45 steps). Open legs also lock margin while the loss grows, and stop-out triggers at a percentage (e.g. 50%), so the broker liquidates while the chain 'still looks recoverable', on the broker's terms at the point of maximum pain.

failure_modes.mode: Undercapitalisation (lot size far too large for the deposit)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: In early July 2026 a well-known grid EA put many users through severe losses within days; the analysis blamed accounts far too small for the exposure the system could take. Vendor guidance for 0.01-lot grids runs $500-$5,000 per pair; $100 at 0.01 standard is 10-50x more leveraged per lot. Later in July, Quantum Queen/OmniGold/Queen X users again reported heavy drawdowns and wiped accounts.

failure_modes.mode: Capping the tail without a gross edge (the 'stopped grid' still bleeds)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: A hard equity stop held over about 1,000 sequences yet the system lost $2,456 in four years with only $128 of costs; a grid's small wins are paid for by the rare huge loss, so removing that loss also removes the profit. Variants with 92-98.5% win rates ended -23.2% and -86.2%. This matches our finding that the symmetric grid has about zero gross edge.

failure_modes.mode: The fatal regime is outside the backtest window
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: In a test of 43 popular gold EAs on 11.5 years of data with default settings, 19% blew up (60-102% equity drawdown). Every account-killer looked strong in recent months and had one fatal drawdown deeper in history that sales pages did not show. Price did not predict safety: the $1,999 EA had PF 0.23 and 99% DD.

failure_modes.mode: Payoff asymmetry hidden by a high win rate
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Averaging refuses every small loss; the rare sequence that never comes back collects all the refused losses at once, multiplied by the grown size. Example: 95% x $2 vs 5% x $45 gives negative expectancy. An average-loss/average-win ratio above 5x means 'the win rate is being bought on credit'.

failure_modes.mode: Lot escalation (martingale or steep per-layer increments), including disguised forms
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Escalation puts the largest positions exactly where losses are already stacking; doubling from 0.01 reaches 1.28 lots after seven losers. At equal profit, a bigger fixed lot had lower DD and one-third to one-half the risk of ruin. 'Smart recovery', 'dynamic lot scaling', 'intelligent position management' and 'hedging recovery' are the same structure under different names.

failure_modes.mode: Fill-triggered escalation in 'semi-HFT' two-sided grids
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: A published Semi-HFT grid seeds 3 stop orders per side, bumps the opposite side after a fill, then switches every pending level to a doubling sequence and adds two more levels once a side has 2 fills, all with no per-trade SL. The faster the market runs one way, the faster size escalates, which is the worst combination for an M1 grid.

failure_modes.mode: Over-optimized grid parameters
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Optimizers converge on a very small gap with a bigger multiplier: baskets close fast and backtest profit looks bigger, but drawdowns and stop-outs grow on other timeframes and periods. The forum consensus is not to optimize the grid part.

failure_modes.mode: Costs and backtest-mode mismatch for micro-scalping grids
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Spread, commission and slippage are a large fraction of a 2-5 pip TP. One trader on a raw account (0.0 spread, $5.5/lot commission) found the system unprofitable once fees were counted. 1-minute OHLC or generated-tick backtests can flip from large profit to large loss on real ticks, and spread-sensitive micro-scalpers are never fully reproduced in the tester.

failure_modes.mode: Night-session edge decay and slippage
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Night scalpers depend on very good trading conditions. Reviews of a well-known EURUSD night scalper report results consistently negative since 2022-2023, slippage problems, and that one bad trade can wipe out one or two months of gains, i.e. the session edge is thin and non-stationary.

failure_modes.mode: News spikes and weekend gaps
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Jumps skip grid levels and fill adds at the worst prices, and the diffusion assumptions behind grid math ignore gaps. This is why BGC forces a Friday flat close and why grid EAs offer 'close all before news'.

failure_modes.mode: Filters that do not cap exposure (including 'ML' filters)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Waka Waka reviewers say its ML pattern filter did not stop it opening trades at extreme levels, which led to deep drawdowns and blown accounts. Entry filters reduce frequency but do not bound loss unless paired with a hard basket stop.

failure_modes.mode: Bi-directional grid: one side fully loaded while the other only takes small TPs
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: In a two-sided grid only one side can be fully allocated at a time. While the losing side is trapped and growing, the winning side keeps banking small TPs, which hides the real net inventory. Without inventory-aware limits the trapped side runs to the stop-out.

failure_modes.mode: Swap accumulation on multi-night holds
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Swap is negligible over an hour but material over several nights. For grids holding baskets for days it can turn a near-zero-edge system negative; this matched our backtest finding.

failure_modes.mode: Fixed-money limits that lose their meaning as the account changes; fragile close logic
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: A fixed $ basket stop is too loose after a drawdown and too tight after growth. Close requests that fail during fast markets or disconnects leave a 'stopped' basket open. This is why protective-close utilities snapshot tickets, retry, check return codes and use percent limits.

notes:
ACCESS LIMITATION, read first. Every WebFetch of www.mql5.com, and of arxiv.org for the Taranto BGC paper, returned EGRESS_BLOCKED from the sandbox proxy. Following the task's fallback rule, ALL evidence here comes from WebSearch result snippets: about 75 targeted searches restricted to mql5.com, each aimed at one specific article, product, blog or thread so snippets could be attributed. "sources_read" therefore means "URLs whose search-result snippets I read", not full-page reads. Quotes and numbers are as the search tool summarized them. Where one search mixed several pages and I could not pin a sentence to one URL (mainly the spread/commission and cent-account items), I list all candidate URLs and mark confidence low. No code was cloned or copied.

STRONGEST, MOST CONSISTENT COMMUNITY LESSONS (each cited above):
(1) Taranto/BGC: open-ended grids head toward almost-sure ruin; finite, restartable cycles (profit target, equity kill switch, age limit, Friday flat) with regime gating are the fix.
(2) Exposure grows as step x N(N-1)/2, and margin stop-out comes before the last level, so size from a pre-trade worst-case simulation.
(3) A hard basket stop prevents ruin but does not create edge; the stopped grid in the 'three gold grids' blog still lost. This agrees with our zero-gross-edge backtest.
(4) Flat or bigger-fixed lots beat escalation at equal profit.
(5) Rolling or partial-close recovery (close the oldest or furthest layer, compensatory trailing) bounds depth.
(6) Session, regime and news gating plus spread/cost floors are where any HF edge has to come from.
(7) The market-making view (Avellaneda-Stoikov) treats the BUY and SELL grids as two quotes with an inventory skew.

INFERENCE: a sketch of the HF $100 EURUSD version of BayesianGrid. All numbers are mine and must be validated in the user's M1 simulator.
- Gates for new cycles: calibrated low-volatility, anti-persistent hours, probably late Asian session, excluding rollover +/- 30-60 min. No high-impact news within 60 min. Spread <= 1.5x that hour's median. M1 Hurst < 0.45 or lag-1 autocorrelation < -0.05. ADX(M15) < 20-25. No CUSUM break and a high sigma/mu on M15-H1. No lock time active after a recent losing stop.
- Spacing: s1 = max(3 pips, k x ATR(M5), 3 x round-trip cost), expanding about 1.25x per level.
- Ladder: flat 0.01 x 3 per side, optional 0.02 on layer 4 only if the pre-trade simulation passes. Max 0.04 lots per side and 0.08 total.
- Worst case per side: about $2.2, i.e. 2.2% of $100, for 3 x 0.01 at 3 / 3.75 pips with a stop one gap beyond.
- TP: the existing live VWAP +/- max(4 x cost, k x ATR), decaying to breakeven plus cost after 10-15 min or at 3+ layers. Trail when there is a single fill. Take a per-layer TP on the newest layer.
- Exits: hard 30-min grid age, closing the whole grid and snapshotting tickets with retries. Per-side basket stop at 2-2.5% equity. Combined both-grid float stop at about 4%. Daily stop at 4-5%. Equity brake 6-8% below the high-water mark. 60-min lock after a losing stop. Friday flat.
- Inventory skew: block adds on the heavy side when |buy lots - sell lots| >= 0.02-0.03, and tighten the light side's TP.
- Optional recovery module: close the oldest loser together with the newest winners when the group net is >= +cost, or a sliding window that closes layer 1 instead of adding layer N+1.
- Costs: a standard-spread account (about 1.3 pips) forces TP >= about 5-6 pips, so 2-3 pip M1 TPs cannot work there. A raw-spread ECN or a cent account (for lot granularity) is strongly preferred. Swap goes to about zero because of the 30-min cap and the pre-rollover cutoff.
- Validation: real-tick or M1 data with commission; walk-forward; must include 2014-15. Do not optimize the ladder, only gates, spacing and TP multiples. Accept a candidate only if the fully stopped version is net positive out of sample, average cycle loss / average cycle win is <= about 4, and the worst cycle is within the pre-trade budget.

Given the community evidence and our own backtests, a profitable HF grid on $100 is not established. The risk stack can bound ruin, but expected value depends on whether the session and regime gates show a real, persistent anti-persistence edge after costs.

findings.mechanism: Hard time barrier on every position or basket (the vertical barrier in the 'triple barrier')
findings.description: In Hummingbot v2 every executor carries a TripleBarrierConfig of stop_loss, take_profit, time_limit and trailing_stop. When time_limit runs out the position is closed with time_limit_order_type, which defaults to MARKET. Both default controllers (market-making and directional) ship with time_limit = 2700 s, i.e. 45 min. The DCA executor counts the deadline from config.timestamp (when the executor was created), not from the first fill. Ilan 1.4 has UseTimeOut/MaxTradeOpenHours (default 48 h), which runs CloseThisSymbolAll(). Freqtrade's custom_exit example sells at a loss once a trade is older than a set age.
findings.evidence: Hummingbot market_making_controller_base: time_limit 2700 s, stop_loss 0.03, take_profit 0.02. directional_trading_controller_base: time_limit 2700, cooldown_time 300, max_executors_per_side 2. position_executor data_types: time_limit_order_type = MARKET. DCA executor: is_expired = timestamp + time_limit. Ilan: MaxTradeOpenHours 48 -> close all.
findings.blowup_protection: Puts a cap on how long a losing inventory can be held. That cuts off the 'hold until it comes back' path that blew every open-ended $100 config in our 2014-15 backtest. The loss becomes a function of how far price can move inside the time window, not of how long a trend lasts.
findings.hf_relevance: This is the core mechanism for the 1-30 min requirement. Inference: the oldest fill (layer 1) is the one that hits the limit first, so measure the basket clock from the FIRST FILL, not grid creation or the last add (Blessing's EEFirstTrade=true does the same). Close the whole grid at market when it reaches 30 min. Also stop adding layers some minutes before the deadline (e.g. no adds after minute 20-25), so the last layers are not opened only to be closed at a loss a few minutes later.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: basket_time_limit = 30 min from first fill (hard). no_new_layers_after = 20-25 min. Close with a market order. Log time-stop exits separately so their share of losses can be optimised.

findings.mechanism: Take-profit that decays over time (and over depth) toward break-even
findings.description: Freqtrade's minimal_roi is a table of the profit required to exit, keyed by minutes since entry. The docs example asks for 4% at 0-20 min, 2% at 20-30, 1% at 30-40 and 0% (break-even) after 40 min. Blessing 3's Early Exit applies EEpc = 1 - EEHoursPC*hours_elapsed - EELevelPC*(level - EEStartLevel) and TP_adjusted = (TP - BE)*EEpc + BE. Defaults: EEStartHours 3, EEHoursPC 0.5%/h, EELevelPC 10%/level. Blessing floors the target at break-even unless EEAllowLoss is set, and can start the clock from the oldest trade (EEFirstTrade). In Avellaneda-Stoikov, as implemented in Hummingbot, the optimal-spread term gamma*sigma*(T-t)/T also shrinks as the horizon runs out.
findings.evidence: Freqtrade docs: keys are minutes since trade.open_date and fees are included. Blessing.mq4 EE formula and defaults. Hummingbot avellaneda_market_making.pyx: spread = gamma*sigma*(T-t)/T + 2/gamma*ln(1+gamma/kappa).
findings.blowup_protection: Exits stale baskets at a small profit or break-even before the hard time stop forces a full loss. More of the 'almost reverted' baskets get closed while they still can be.
findings.hf_relevance: Fits the user's single shared TP (VWAP +/- TP_Pips) directly: make TP_Pips a function of basket age and layer count. Inference: TP(t) = max(BE_plus_costs, TP0*(1 - t/T_decay)) with T_decay about 15-25 min, then the hard 30-min stop. 'BE' has to include the spread already paid plus commission, or the decayed TP still loses money.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: TP0 = 1.0-1.5x current spacing. Decay to BE+0.3 pip of costs by minute 15-20. From layer >= N-1 jump straight to BE (see the break-even-level finding). Freqtrade-style table, e.g. {0: TP0, 10: 0.6*TP0, 20: costs, 30: hard close}.

findings.mechanism: Grid spacing scaled by volatility (ATR, NATR, Bollinger width or log-range EMA), with floor and ceiling clamps
findings.description:
Volatility scaling of spacing appears across almost all the better-built bots:
- GridMaster Pro: spacing = ATR(14, chart TF)*1.5.
- Zerith mean-reversion EA: step = clamp(ATR_M15*1.4, $3.50, $12).
- GoldHedgerPro v4: distance = clamp(ATR(14, M20)*1.3, 80..250 pips).
- Ghost Grid Eye: grid = ATR(14)*0.80 and SL = 2.0*ATR on M1.
- Blessing AutoCal: ATR is multiplied by 2/4/8/12 as the grid moves into deeper 'sets'.
- Hummingbot pmm_dynamic: spread multiplier = NATR(14)/100 on 3-min candles.
- Hummingbot DMan V3: spread multiplier = BB_width/200, and stop/trailing scale with it when dynamic_target is on.
- Hummingbot PositionExecutor.new_instance_with_adjusted_volatility(): scales SL/TP/trailing by a volatility factor and deliberately leaves time_limit alone.
- passivbot v8: volatility = EMA(ln(high/low)) on 1m and 1h, which widens the entry threshold multiplicatively.
findings.evidence: Formulas as cited. passivbot: effective_threshold = base*max(1, 1 + we_ratio*we_w + vol_1h*w1h + vol_1m*w1m).
findings.blowup_protection: In fast markets the grid widens, so a fixed number of layers covers more price before the ladder is full, and the loss per pip of move per layer is spread over a wider distance. The clamps stop the grid from becoming too dense in dead markets, where cost per fill dominates.
findings.hf_relevance: The user's 7.5-pip fixed spacing assumes one regime. For M1/M5 holding of 1-30 min, scale off short-horizon volatility: ATR(M1, 14-60) or passivbot-style EMA(ln(H/L)) on 1m. Keep a cost floor (see the next finding). Inference: an ATR measured on the same timeframe as entries reacts quickly but is noisy. A blend of 1m and 1h (as passivbot does) avoids spacing collapsing right before a breakout.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference for EURUSD: spacing = clamp(k*ATR_M1(30), max(4*spread, 2.5 pip), 10 pip) with k in 1.5-3. Optimise k walk-forward. Freeze spacing for the life of a basket (compute at first fill), as Blessing and martin-binance compute at cycle start, so the ladder geometry stays known.

findings.mechanism: Spacing and TP floored by trading cost (spread + commission), set as multiples of cost
findings.description: Xtley001's 'High-Frequency Grid EA' expresses every distance as a multiple of AverageSpread, where AverageSpread = max(SpreadMultiplier*Point, CurrentSpread + CommissionPerPip). Order distance = AverageSpread*Delta (0.5), max distance = AverageSpread*7, SL = AverageSpread*10, trailing = AverageSpread*4. GoldHedgerPro v4 only enters when spread <= 15% of the computed grid distance and pauses adds when spread is above its cap. martin-binance says PROFIT should be > 2*FEE_MAKER and builds fees into the TP price (calc_profit_order, fee_for_tp). Hummingbot PMM has add_transaction_costs. GridPilot is maker-first, using taker only when the deviation exceeds about 2x the fee spread.
findings.evidence: Xtley mq5 formulas; GoldHedgerPro gate 'spread must be <=15% of calculated grid distance'; martin-binance template comment 'recommended FEE_MAKER*2<PROFIT<=0.85'.
findings.blowup_protection: Stops the grid from paying a spread that eats most of each TP. With a symmetric grid that has no gross edge, the spread is the guaranteed bleed, and it grows with the number of fills.
findings.hf_relevance: This decides whether the EA can work at 1-30 min on a $100 standard account. A 1.0-1.5 pip retail EURUSD spread against a 2-5 pip TP means 25-60% of gross is lost to cost. Inference: on a standard account, require TP_net >= 3x spread and spacing >= 4x spread. Strongly prefer a raw-spread/ECN account, where round-turn cost is about 0.7-0.9 pip. Block trading when spread/ATR_M1 is above a threshold (rollover, thin hours).
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: max_spread_to_spacing = 0.15-0.25 (from GoldHedgerPro). max_spread_abs = 1.5x median session spread. Use the live, per-session spread, not a constant.

findings.mechanism: Where a professional HF grid's edge comes from: maker rebates plus short-horizon mean reversion, under a hard position limit
findings.description: hftbacktest's HF grid has 20 levels per side, grid_interval = 10 ticks and half_spread = 20 ticks, re-quotes every 100 ms and caps max_position = 5. On ETHUSDT (5 days, Oct 2022) it reports +8.27% return, Sharpe 18.27, max DD 2.19%, about 9,490 trades/day. The cross-exchange notebook says verbatim: 'All backtests are based on a 0.005% rebate, the highest market maker rebate available on Binance Futures.' and 'Without alpha, this relies heavily on rebates combined with short-term mean reversion to the current price — a behavior that has been observed to be particularly strong in altcoins.'
findings.evidence: Verbatim quotes from the notebook. Results from the HF grid notebook. algo.rs: orders only post while position < max_position (bids) or > -max_position (asks).
findings.blowup_protection: The professional version survives through a strict max_position (inventory cap), constant re-quoting, and being paid (rebate) rather than paying for each fill.
findings.hf_relevance: This matches our backtest result: the unfiltered symmetric grid has about zero gross edge, and spread/swap make it negative. A retail MT5 grid using market orders pays the spread on every fill and gets no rebate, so the institutional HF-grid economics do not carry over. Inference: the user's version needs an actual alpha (stretch/mean-reversion entry, regime filter, session selection) plus a cost floor. Without them, faster holding only increases the number of spread payments.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: before building, measure on M1 data the gross expectancy per fill of the entry signal net of spread. If it is below spread + commission, no ladder or lot scheme will fix it.

findings.mechanism: Exposure cap (wallet-exposure limit) as the main sizing constraint, rather than layer count
findings.description: passivbot defines wallet_exposure = position_size*avg_entry/unleveraged_balance. Each position has wallet_exposure_limit = total_wallet_exposure_limit/n_positions, and the bot stops adding once WEL is reached. Further layers: an entry gate on total exposure (TWEL), enforcers that trim positions above effective_limit*threshold (e.g. 0.9-1.05), and a total-exposure enforcer that reduces profitable positions first, then the shallowest losses. The doc gives the bankruptcy distances: WE 2 -> 50% adverse move, WE 3 -> 33%, WE 10 -> 10%. Other examples: hftbacktest max_position; Zerith max single lot 0.10 and max cumulative 0.25 lots; AS-Grid POSITION_THRESHOLD; Hummingbot grid executor max_open_orders.
findings.evidence: passivbot risk_management.md formulas and enforcer policies. Exchange leverage must exceed TWEL_long + TWEL_short.
findings.blowup_protection: The worst case is bounded by notional exposure, so the distance to ruin is known up front: ruin move ~ 1/WE. Layer-count caps alone do not do this when lots grow.
findings.hf_relevance: For $100: 0.01 lot EURUSD is about 1,000 EUR notional, so WE ~ 11 per 0.01 lot at 1.10. 0.08 lots is WE ~ 90, and a ~1.1% (about 120 pip) move wipes the account. Inference: express MaxTotalLots as max_WE, i.e. max total notional / equity. For a 30-min hold, size so that (total lots) x (2-sigma 30-min move + spacing depth) <= the risk budget. EURUSD's 30-min 2-sigma is very roughly 10-20 pips in active sessions; measure it on the user's M1 data.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: on a $100 account, max total lots across both grids ~0.04-0.06 (WE ~ 45-65). Per-grid cap ~0.03-0.04. Keep a margin-level freeze (Zerith freezes new levels at margin level <200% and cuts the worst position at <120%).

findings.mechanism: Ladder budget allocated in advance (sizes derived from a fixed total budget, not added one layer at a time)
findings.description: martin-binance sizes the grid geometrically so that the whole deposit is used across ORDER_Q orders: amount_i = depo*m^i*(m-1)/(m^ORDER_Q - 1), with m = (100+MARTIN)/100 and MARTIN in 5-20%. Only GRID_MAX_COUNT orders sit on the exchange at once; the rest are held back. Hummingbot's DCAExecutorConfig takes the full amounts_quote[] and prices[] lists at creation, so total exposure is known before the first fill. Freqtrade's DCA example stakes 1, 1.25, 1.5 and 1.75x of a base and sets max_dca_multiplier = 5.5, so the initial stake is the budget divided by 5.5.
findings.evidence: martin-binance executor.py volume formula. Template: ORDER_Q 12, MARTIN 10, GRID_MAX_COUNT 5. Freqtrade docs: max_entry_position_adjustment = 3 and the 5.5 multiplier.
findings.blowup_protection: The worst-case loss of a full ladder (sum of lots x distance to the basket stop) becomes a design input. The user's current ladder is defined bottom-up (BaseLot + LotIncrement per layer), so its total exposure is only an emergent result.
findings.hf_relevance: Directly usable. Pick the basket risk budget first (e.g. 3-5% of equity), the layer count and the stop distance, then solve for the lots. With 0.01 as the broker minimum on $100, the solution will usually be flat 0.01 lots for 3-5 layers. Inference: on $100, progression above 0.01 per layer cannot fit a 3-5% budget beyond 4-5 layers at 3-5 pip spacing.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference, worked example: 4 layers x 0.01 at 0/3/6/9 pips puts the average 4.5 pips from L1. A stop 5 pips past the last layer (14 pips from L1) loses 0.04 lots x 9.5 pips x $10/lot-pip = $3.8, about 3.8% of $100. Adding a 0.02 fifth layer at 12 pips with a stop at 17 pips gives about $7.4.

findings.mechanism: Total grid depth bounded by a statistical range, with a basket stop once the ladder is full
findings.description: martin-binance sets the total 'overlap' (grid depth) adaptively: over_price = max(100*(base - BB_lower)/base, ATR*K_ATR/base*100), with KBB = 2 on 20 x 60-min candles. The ladder therefore spans about a 2-sigma band, and profit is clamped between PROFIT and PROFIT_MAX. Hummingbot's DCA executor in MAKER mode only arms its stop loss once all levels are filled; TAKER mode stops on net_pnl_quote <= -max_loss_quote. Hummingbot's grid executor exits on position pnl% <= -stop_loss, or on a limit_price (BUY grid exits if mid <= limit_price).
findings.evidence: martin-binance set_trade_conditions and set_profit. dca_executor control logic. grid_executor control_triple_barrier: SL, then limit price, then time limit, then trailing, then TP.
findings.blowup_protection: Once price has moved beyond what the ladder was built to absorb (about a 2-sigma excursion), the grid stops averaging and realises a bounded loss instead of turning into a martingale.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: set total ladder depth to the 1.5-2 sigma excursion over the 30-min holding window (measured on M1, per session). Place the basket stop at depth + one spacing. If the move exceeds that inside 30 min, the regime is trending, and the grid should lose a small known amount.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: depth = z*sigma_30min*sqrt(...) with z in 1.5-2.0, and layers = floor(depth/spacing), typically 3-5. Basket stop = 1 spacing past the last layer, or a money stop of 3-5% of equity, whichever hits first.

findings.mechanism: 'Stop-loss grid': a hard level-count stop that accepts small losses in exchange for no unbounded drawdown
findings.description: Orchard Forex's Stop Loss Grid (based on the Expert4x approach) halts after 4 level iterations ('if (mLevelCount >= 4)': 'Hit SL, stopping expert'). The README says it 'removes the possibility of unlimited drawdowns in the case of a strong trend but does introduce losses at the stop loss point.' Other per-position or basket hard stops: Ghost Grid Eye uses BasketStopLossMoney $5 and a hard SL of ATR*2 on every trade. Zerith uses an emergency SL of 3.5 x H1 ATR from the first entry. GoldHedgerPro uses a 500-pip emergency SL on every position so a disconnect is covered (Blessing's UsePowerOutSL/POSLPips 600 serves the same purpose).
findings.evidence: Code and README as quoted.
findings.blowup_protection: Turns the grid's tail risk (rare total loss) into a frequent, small, known cost.
findings.hf_relevance: The user's EA has no per-position SL. Inference: add (a) a basket money stop, (b) a level-count stop after the last layer, and (c) a broker-side catastrophic SL on every position at depth + a buffer, so a VPS or connection failure does not leave a $100 account naked during a news spike.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: broker-side SL at about basket stop + 5 pips. Basket stop 3-5% of equity. Halt new grids after K consecutive basket stops (see the cooldown finding).

findings.mechanism: Inventory skew: size and price of the two sides tilted by net inventory
findings.description: Hummingbot PMM's inventory_skew_calculator values the portfolio, caps the allowed band at 50% of value, and interpolates the current base inventory between [left limit, target] -> [0, 0.5] and [target, right limit] -> [0.5, 1.0]. That maps to a bid size multiplier in [2.0 .. 0.0]; the ask multiplier is 2 minus the bid multiplier. Parameters: inventory_target_base_pct (default 50%) and inventory_range_multiplier (default 1). Hummingbot's Avellaneda implementation shifts the reservation price by q*gamma*sigma*(T-t)/T, with q = (balance - target)/total inventory, and shrinks the size of the inventory-increasing side by e^(-eta*q). hftbacktest's grid uses bid_depth = half_spread + skew*position/order_qty and ask_depth = half_spread - skew*position/order_qty: a long position pushes bids further away and pulls asks closer. GLFT (in the hftbacktest tutorial) derives half-spread c1 and skew q*sigma*c2 from fitted trade intensity (A, k) and volatility.
findings.evidence: Code formulas as cited. GLFT: delta_b = c1 + (Delta/2)*sigma*c2 + q*sigma*c2.
findings.blowup_protection: Inventory that drifts in one direction makes the bot less willing to add to it and more eager to unload it. This slows the run-away accumulation that ruins grids in a trend.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference for the user's two magic-isolated grids on a hedging account: define net inventory q = BuyGridLots - SellGridLots. When q is large, (1) scale down further adds on the heavy grid (multiplier -> 0 at the range limit), (2) scale up the base lot of the next opposite-grid start (up to 2x, which acts as a natural partial hedge), and (3) pull the heavy grid's shared TP closer (smaller TP_Pips), which is the reservation-price shift. All of this has to stay under the total-exposure cap, and each hedge leg pays spread.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: add-size multiplier on the heavy side = clamp(1 - |q|/q_max, 0, 1). Opposite-side starter multiplier = 1 + |q|/q_max (max 2). TP shift = -skew*|q|/0.01 pips with skew ~0.2-0.5 pip per 0.01 lot of imbalance.

findings.mechanism: Inventory thresholds: double-size TP, then 'lockdown' (no more adds), then emergency reduction of both sides
findings.description:
AS-Grid (a dual-side long and short futures grid, structurally like the user's BUY and SELL grids) works in tiers:
- Normal: TP at +GRID_SPACING (0.4%) and adds at -GRID_SPACING, using INITIAL_QUANTITY.
- Above POSITION_LIMIT: TP quantity is doubled to unload faster.
- Above POSITION_THRESHOLD: no new orders on that side ('lockdown'); only the TP stays, plus a 60 s cooldown.
- When BOTH sides are >= 0.8 x POSITION_THRESHOLD: reduce-only market reductions of 0.1 x threshold per batch, with a cooldown and at most 3 triggers per day.
Unfilled orders older than 300 s are cancelled.
findings.evidence: gate_bot.py defaults: GRID_SPACING 0.004, POSITION_THRESHOLD = 10*qty/spacing*2/100 (500 contracts), POSITION_LIMIT 250, ORDER_COOLDOWN_TIME 60 s, order timeout 300 s.
findings.blowup_protection: Caps inventory per side and unwinds the 'both legs loaded' state of a hedged grid instead of letting it consume margin and swap indefinitely.
findings.hf_relevance: The user runs two independent grids on a hedging account, so both can be loaded after a whipsaw. Inference: add (a) a per-grid lockdown lot level (stop adding, keep TP), (b) a rule for when both grids are deep (close the worse layers of both, or flatten both when the combined float < -X%), and (c) a cap on how many emergency reductions per day before trading halts.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: lockdown at 75% of the per-grid lot cap. Both-sides-deep trigger when each grid >= 0.8x cap. Max 2-3 emergency events per day, then halt until the next session.

findings.mechanism: Partial de-risking: close the worst or oldest layers using profits ('auto-unstuck', close-oldest, layered stop buffer)
findings.description: passivbot auto-unstuck: when position_exposure/effective_WEL > unstuck.threshold and price reaches EMA_band*(1 +/- ema_dist), it makes partial loss-taking closes of unstuck.close_pct of the budget. These are paced by a loss allowance: loss_floor = balance_peak*(1 - loss_allowance_pct*TWEL). passivbot's docs admit that 'Extreme black-swan events may cause the auto-unstuck mechanism to keep taking losses and re-entering continually.' Blessing's UseCloseOldest closes the oldest trade once CloseTradesLevel (5) trades are open and it is in profit. GridPilot replaces one-shot liquidation with a 'stop buffer zone' that reduces the position level by level with limit orders before a final emergency stop. GoldHedgerPro's margin-emergency rule cuts the worst single position when margin level < 120%.
findings.evidence: passivbot configuration.md and risk_management.md formulas; Blessing defaults; GridPilot README; GoldHedgerPro inputs.
findings.blowup_protection: Lowers exposure gradually, funded by realised gains, before a full stop is needed. The loss allowance tied to peak balance caps the total cost of unsticking.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: with a 30-min hard stop, a full unstuck engine is less important. A simple version still helps: at layer >= N-1, when the basket's realised profit since the grid started (or the session's realised profit) covers it, close the deepest layer first. That lowers the VWAP and moves TP closer. Take care that it does not turn into loss-recycling.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: allow at most 1-2 partial reductions per basket. Cap total realised loss from reductions at 1% of balance_peak per day (passivbot-style loss_allowance).

findings.mechanism: Break-even exit once a deep level is reached, and closes that get more eager as exposure grows
findings.description: Blessing 3's BreakEvenTrade (default 12, with MaxTrades 15) closes the whole basket at break-even once that level is reached, without waiting for TP. passivbot's close threshold is additive: effective_threshold = base + we_ratio*we_weight + vol terms. A negative threshold_we_weight makes closes more eager as wallet exposure grows. Hummingbot grid executor's coerce_tp_to_step sets TP = max(step, configured TP) so the exit sits on the grid geometry.
findings.evidence: Blessing inputs; passivbot configuration.md close-threshold formula.
findings.blowup_protection: A deep basket carries the most tail risk, so its required reversion should be the smallest. Exiting flat at depth avoids the last, most dangerous leg.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: the user's shared TP = VWAP +/- 5.3 pips is the same at every depth, but the dollar risk at layer 5 is several times that at layer 1. Make TP_Pips shrink with layer count, reaching break-even plus costs at layer >= N-1. Combine with the time decay.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: TP_pips(level) = TP0*(1 - 0.15*(level-1)), floored at costs. BE-exit at level >= N-1.

findings.mechanism: Equity hard stop and drawdown tiers with cooldown, smoothing and a restart policy
findings.description: passivbot's HSL: red_threshold is a drawdown from peak (e.g. 0.10). The signal is the minimum of raw episode drawdown and its EMA (ema_span_minutes). On RED it blocks entries, makes panic closes (limit or market), waits cooldown_minutes_after_red, then follows restart_after_red_policy = always|never. Scope can be coin, side or unified. GoldHedgerPro has three layers: 10% DD closes all, a 15% drop from the equity peak closes all and pauses 24 h, and a 3% daily loss closes all until midnight. GridMaster Pro closes all and pauses at a 5% equity DD. Ilan has UseEquityStop/TotalEquityRisk 20%. Blessing has StopTradePercent 10 (stops new trades) and MaxDDPercent 50% of the allocated 'portion' (closes all). Freqtrade's MaxDrawdown protection uses calculation_mode 'equity', lookback 48 candles, max_allowed_drawdown 0.2 and stops for 12 candles.
findings.evidence: Docs and code parameters as listed.
findings.blowup_protection: Caps the loss for a whole episode, not just a basket, and forces a pause so the bot is not restarting into the same regime that just hit it.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference for $100: two levels. (1) Daily loss limit of about 3-5% closes everything and halts until the next session or day. (2) Equity-peak drawdown of 10-15% halts for 24-72 h or requires a manual restart. Use equity including floating P/L, anchored to a rolling peak, not the EA start balance (GridMaster's anchor bug).
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: daily_loss = 4%, peak_DD_halt = 12% with restart='never' (manual), and smooth the trigger with a short EMA only if spikes cause false triggers.

findings.mechanism: Cooldowns after stops and losses (consecutive-loss guard, StoplossGuard, post-close delay)
findings.description: Ghost Grid Eye: after MaxConsecutiveLosses = 3 it freezes for CooldownMinutes = 30, and DailyLossLimitMoney $20 blocks entries for the rest of the day. Freqtrade protections: StoplossGuard (e.g. 4 stoplosses within 24 candles locks trading for 4 candles), CooldownPeriod (no re-entry for N candles after an exit), and LowProfitPairs (lock a pair whose profit < 2% over 6 candles, for 60 candles). Hummingbot directional controllers use cooldown_time 300 s between executors. The MM controller keeps a level filtered for 15 s after a stop-loss. PMM's filled_order_delay defaults to 60 s. Zerith waits 15 min after a basket close.
findings.evidence: Parameters as cited.
findings.blowup_protection: Consecutive basket stops are themselves evidence of a regime change (trend or news). A forced pause stops the EA from restarting a grid into the same move.
findings.hf_relevance: The user's EA restarts both grids on every new M15 bar when idle. Inference: on M1/M5, after a basket hard-stop or time-stop at a loss, block that direction's grid for 15-60 min. After 2-3 losing baskets in a session, stop until the next session.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: cooldown_after_loss = 15-30 min per direction. Session stop after 2 consecutive basket stops. Post-TP delay of 1-3 bars to avoid restarting into the same micro-swing.

findings.mechanism: Trend-regime gate on starting new grids (ADX/DI, EMA separation, Mann-Kendall test, multi-indicator regime)
findings.description: martin-binance's TRADE_CONTROL delays the start of a cycle in a strong adverse trend. It uses multi-timeframe +DI minus -DI, ADX_THRESHOLD 40 on 1-min candles, ADX period 14, and a Mann-Kendall trend-significance test before releasing (TC_DI_DIFF 5). Zerith blocks entries when H1 ADX(14) > 28 or when the EMA50/EMA200 separation is too large, and forces an 'escape' (closes the basket) at ADX >= 32 with trend confirmation. GoldHedgerPro only trades in the direction of the H1 EMA50. Ladder-Dragon classifies regimes with ATR, EMA, VWAP and ADX before laddering. Blessing has MAEntry and ForceMarketCond (auto range/trend detection). arbitrage-grid-bot is a naive version: direction comes from an H1 MA(50).
findings.evidence: Code and README parameters as listed.
findings.blowup_protection: A grid's losses come almost entirely from trends. Not starting, or escaping, when a trend is statistically present removes the worst baskets.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: for 1-30 min holding, filter on an M5-M15 trend measure, not H1-D1 (too slow to matter within 30 min). Options include ADX(M5, 14) > 25-30, |EMA20 slope| on M5 > k*ATR, or a Mann-Kendall/variance-ratio test on the last 30-60 M1 returns. When a trend is present, either skip both grids, or run only the with-trend grid with no adds (a hybrid many of these EAs use).
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: ADX_M5 threshold 25-30. Escape: close the counter-trend basket if ADX_M5 > 35 and the basket is losing. Use closed bars only (as Ghost Grid does) to avoid repainting.

findings.mechanism: Entry on a stretch from a mean, confirmed by reversion, instead of 'open both grids every new bar'
findings.description:
Several open-source systems only start a grid after price has stretched away from a mean:
- Zerith: M15 RSI < 35 AND price at the lower BB(20, 2.0) for buys; mirrored for sells.
- Hummingbot DMan V3: long when BBP < 0, short when BBP > 1, with BB(100, 2.0).
- Blessing: optional Bollinger, Stochastic, CCI or MACD entries.
- passivbot: the initial entry is gated by EMA bands (ema_span_0/1). A long only starts at lower band - initial_ema_dist, and with retracement_base_pct > 0 the bot waits for an excursion and then a pullback.
- GridPilot 'trailing entry': follows price down and enters only after a confirmed rebound (default 0.2%).
- Ghost Grid Eye: 'sweep-and-reclaim'. Price must penetrate a level by >= 0.05 ATR, reclaim by >= 0.05 ATR, and pass a composite score >= 60, with an ADX/DI regime component.
- GoldHedgerPro: liquidity-sweep detection (wick >= 15 pips, body < 40% of range, break-of-structure confirmation).
findings.evidence: Parameters as cited.
findings.blowup_protection: Starting the grid closer to an extreme makes the first layers more likely to revert. The trailing or reclaim confirmation avoids catching the knife in the middle of an impulse.
findings.hf_relevance: Our backtest shows the symmetric 'both grids on each bar' start has about zero gross edge. Inference: use a stretch trigger on M1/M5 and only start the grid on the side opposite the stretch. Examples: z = (close - EMA_or_VWAP)/sigma >= 1.5-2.5, or a BB(20-100) band touch, followed by a 1-bar reclaim. That turns the grid from a pure inventory machine into a mean-reversion scalper with a measurable signal.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: z-score on M1 with a 60-120-bar EMA or session VWAP, entry |z| >= 2. Confirmation is the first M1 close back inside the band. Signal validity 3-5 bars (Ghost Grid's EyeSignalTimeoutMinutes 45 is a similar idea).

findings.mechanism: Momentum and retracement confirmation before each ADD ('SmartGrid', re-entry gating, exposure-weighted thresholds)
findings.description: Blessing SmartGrid (default true) checks RSI against its moving average before placing the next level, so adds are delayed while momentum still runs against the basket. passivbot can gate re-entries by EMA bands (ema_gate_mode 'all' or 'reentry'), can require a favourable excursion and then a retracement before re-entry, and widens the re-entry threshold multiplicatively with the wallet-exposure ratio (threshold_we_weight) and with 1m/1h volatility. Hummingbot's grid executor limits adds through order_frequency (minimum seconds between new orders), max_orders_per_batch and activation_bounds (levels are only placed within mid*(1 +/- bounds)).
findings.evidence: Blessing inputs. passivbot formula effective_threshold = base*max(1, 1 + we_ratio*we_w + ...). Grid executor get_open_orders_to_create filters.
findings.blowup_protection: In an impulse, a fixed-distance grid fills every layer within minutes. Confirmation and minimum time between adds spread the fills out, so the hard time stop or regime filter can act before the ladder is full.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: on M1, require at least one M1 bar between adds and a non-adverse close (or RSI(M1) turning). Widen the next spacing by (1 + w*exposure_ratio). Pause adds entirely while a news window is active (already in the user's v6.13).
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: min_seconds_between_adds = 60-180. we_weight 0.5-1.0 (spacing grows 50-100% as the grid nears its cap).

findings.mechanism: Spacing that widens with depth (grid sets, logarithmic or expanding grids)
findings.description: Blessing uses SetCountArray '4,4', GridSetArray '25,50,100' and TP_SetArray '50,100,200': the first block of layers is tight and later blocks are wider, with their own TPs. With AutoCal the multipliers become ATR x2/x4/x8/x12. martin-binance spaces levels as price_k = 1 - log(order_q - i, order_q + LINEAR_GRID_K), giving logarithmic density near the base (default LINEAR_GRID_K 50). Orchard's 'expanding grid' is a 'Martingale grid with levels growing as more levels added'.
findings.evidence: Code and README as cited.
findings.blowup_protection: For the same number of layers, the deeper layers cover more price, so the ladder fills up more slowly in a trend. That buys time for the time stop or regime escape.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: on M1/M5, use something like spacing_i = s0*(1 + g*(i-1)) with g 0.25-0.5, so layers 1-2 harvest micro noise and layers 4-5 sit near the 2-sigma 30-min extreme. Combine with flat or slowly growing lots. Widening and growing lots together is how the exposure math gets out of hand.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: s0 = 1.5-2x ATR_M1. g = 0.3-0.5. 4-5 layers max.

findings.mechanism: Lot progression shape and hard caps (per level and in total)
findings.description:
The catalogue covers the full range of progressions:
- Ilan 1.4: LotExponent 1.667, MaxTrades 10. Naive and decompiled.
- Blessing: Multiplier 1.4, MaxTrades 15.
- Springfield 3 Grids: LotsExponent, i.e. last lot x coefficient.
- jumpycalm cBot: VolumeExponent 1.0 (flat) by default, MaxOpenBuy/Sell 8.
- GoldHedgerPro: 1.5x, max 4 positions per side.
- martin-binance: MARTIN 5-20% per order.
- passivbot: double_down_factor, where next qty = position size x factor.
- Freqtrade example: linear additive 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75.
- arbitrage-grid-bot: additive (1x, 2x, 3x) or multiplicative (1x, 2x, 4x).
Caps: Zerith max single lot 0.10 and max cumulative 0.25. GoldHedgerPro InpVolMultiplierCap 5.0. User EA MaxTotalLots 8.0.
findings.evidence: Inputs as cited.
findings.blowup_protection: Only the caps bound the loss; the progression shape only changes how fast the cap is reached. Geometric progressions (>= 1.4) put most exposure in the last 2-3 layers, which is exactly where the loss is realised in a trend.
findings.hf_relevance: The user asks for 'start 0.01 and scale up per layer'. On $100 the minimum lot step (0.01) makes any growth coarse: 0.01 -> 0.02 doubles the risk. Inference: flat 0.01 for layers 1-3, then at most one step to 0.02 on the last 1-2 layers, with total lots <= 0.06 and the full-ladder stop loss <= 5% of equity. Scale BaseLot only with equity (Blessing PortionPC / UseMM style), not with depth.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: ladder [0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.02, (0.02)]. Max total per grid 0.07. Combined across both grids 0.08-0.10 only if the basket stop math still fits the budget. Recompute when equity doubles.

findings.mechanism: News filter that also freezes ADDS, with a volatility-based 'settle' before resuming
findings.description:
GoldHedgerPro v4.2:
- Blocks new entries starting 30 min before high-impact USD/EUR events (importance 3).
- Optionally flattens the active basket before the news (InpFlattenBeforeNews).
- After the event, waits at least 15 min, then resumes only when ATR <= 1.3x the pre-event baseline, with a hard maximum block of 120 min.
Its changelog explains why: v4.01 blocked only new entries, and 'the martingale kept averaging into spikes (e.g., FOMC) with zero awareness'. The fix blocks grid additions for the whole news window.
findings.evidence: GoldHedgerPro_v4.mq5 inputs and version notes.
findings.blowup_protection: News spikes are the fastest way to fill a whole ladder within minutes. Freezing adds and requiring volatility to normalise prevents averaging into the impulse.
findings.hf_relevance: Consistent with our finding that a news filter plus pausing adds cut drawdowns materially. Inference: for a 30-min max hold, consider flattening (or only allowing TP/BE exits) for open baskets that would otherwise be held through the release, since the time stop will not save a basket during a 30-pip spike. Resume on an ATR-settle condition instead of a fixed timer.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: block new grids from T-30 to T+15 (min). Flatten or BE-exit baskets at T-5 when float < 0. Resume when ATR_M1(14) <= 1.3x the pre-news median, capped at T+120.

findings.mechanism: Session profiles: different thresholds, ATR multipliers and position caps per session, with management always active
findings.description:
GoldHedgerPro sets per-session ADX minimum, volume threshold, ATR multiplier and max positions:
- Asian 00-08 GMT: disabled.
- London 08-13: ADX 20, ATR x1.3, max 4.
- Overlap 13-17: ADX 18, ATR x1.5, max 5.
- NY close 17-21: ADX 25, max 3.
It also blocks holidays and stops new entries in the last 90 min on Friday. Zerith trades 07-21 UTC with a Friday cutoff at 18:00 and optional Asian-night avoidance. Ghost Grid Eye allows entries 01-22 server time, while 'position management (basket close, breakeven, trailing) always active regardless of session'. Hummingbot Avellaneda has execution_timeframe_mode daily_between_times. Blessing has UseHolidayShutdown.
findings.evidence: Inputs as cited.
findings.blowup_protection: Gating by session avoids thin-liquidity and rollover periods (wide spreads and gaps) and lets risk caps tighten in sessions prone to trends.
findings.hf_relevance: The user already gates new grids by hour. Inference: make spacing multiplier, max layers and entry z-threshold session-dependent, and keep exit management (TP decay, time stop, basket stop) running 24/5. For EURUSD M1, avoid rollover (about 21:00-23:00 GMT, wide spreads). Test the Asian range (mean-reverting, but small ATR versus spread) and London/NY (more ATR, more trend) separately in the M1 backtest rather than assuming either is better.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: per-session table of {enabled, z_entry, spacing_k, max_layers, max_lots}, optimised walk-forward. No new grids in the 30 min before session close or before Friday close.

findings.mechanism: Order refresh, staleness and grid re-anchoring (order_refresh_time, max_order_age, grid shift, hanging orders)
findings.description: Hummingbot PMM settings: order_refresh_time (cancel and replace on a cycle), max_order_age 1800 s (refresh even at the same price), order_refresh_tolerance_pct and filled_order_delay 60 s. Hanging orders keep the unfilled side of a pair after a fill and cancel it if |price - current|/current > hanging_orders_cancel_pct (10%); they are renewed after max_order_age with no aggregation. The MM controller refreshes executors after executor_refresh_time (300 s). hftbacktest re-quotes every 100 ms and cancels orders outside the new grid. martin-binance re-anchors the grid (grid_update) if price runs more than max(PRICE_SHIFT, 0.25*ATR%) before the first fill, after SHIFT_GRID_DELAY 15 s. AS-Grid cancels unfilled orders after 300 s.
findings.evidence: Code and config as cited.
findings.blowup_protection: Stale resting orders get filled at prices that no longer reflect the current regime. Refreshing and re-anchoring keep the inventory tied to current conditions.
findings.hf_relevance: The user's EA adds at market when price crosses a spacing, so resting-order staleness is not an issue. The equivalent risk is a stale grid ORIGIN. Inference: if a grid's first layer has not reached TP within N minutes and price has drifted, the decaying TP and the time stop already handle it. For pending-order variants, apply a max_order_age of about 5-15 min.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: re-anchor or cancel unfilled pending layers after 10 min. filled_order_delay-style pause of 1-3 min after a TP before restarting that side.

findings.mechanism: Basket trailing take-profit (lock in after a money target, exit on giveback)
findings.description: GoldHedgerPro: once the basket reaches InpBasketProfitUSD $4, it tracks the high-water mark and closes if profit retreats 30%. Zerith: basket trailing starts at $10 profit with a $3 step, and the exit is hybrid (whichever hits first of 0.5% of balance, $15, or VWAP +/- 0.3 x ATR). Blessing: MaximizeProfit with ProfitSet 70% of potential, MoveTP 30 and TotalMoves 2. Hummingbot: TrailingStop(activation_price, trailing_delta) on net P&L%. Freqtrade: trailing_stop_positive 0.02 with offset 0.03 and trailing_only_offset_is_reached.
findings.evidence: Inputs as cited.
findings.blowup_protection: Mostly about profit capture rather than ruin. It can shorten exposure time once a basket is in profit.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: for 1-30 min mean reversion, trailing usually reduces the average win (reversion moves stall at the mean). Test it against a fixed decaying TP before adopting it. A useful variant: once the basket is net-positive by about 1x spread after minute 10-15, trail tightly so it exits before the hard time stop.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: activate at TP0*0.7 and close on a 30% giveback, as an A/B test against a plain TP.

findings.mechanism: Capped open orders, entry frequency and concurrent executors per side
findings.description: Hummingbot GridExecutor: max_open_orders (default 5; GridStrike default 2), max_orders_per_batch (1), order_frequency (s), and activation_bounds that place only levels near mid. GridStrike only creates a new grid executor when none is active and mid is inside [start_price, end_price]. The directional controller caps max_executors_per_side = 2 with a 300 s cooldown. Ghost Grid Eye allows a single managed position at a time.
findings.evidence: Code as cited.
findings.blowup_protection: Stops the bot from stacking several overlapping grids in one direction, which is a hidden multiplier on exposure.
findings.hf_relevance: The user isolates one BUY and one SELL grid by magic number, which is correct. Inference: keep it strictly at one basket per direction. Do not restart a direction while its previous basket is still open. Rate-limit adds per minute.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: max 1 basket per side, at most 1 add per M1 bar, and grid restarts limited to 1 per 5-15 min per side.

findings.mechanism: Allocated capital 'portion' and recovery-at-reduced-size (handle with care)
findings.description: Blessing's PortionPC sets the share of the account the EA trades. Lots and MaxDD scale from PortionBalance, and PortionChange can grow the portion at new highs. GoldHedgerPro's recovery mode: after a 10% DD close-all, it runs 5 recovery baskets at 0.5x lots. The source review flags this as a weakness because five half-size baskets can still pile up losses in a sustained trend.
findings.evidence: Inputs as cited.
findings.blowup_protection: PortionPC limits what the grid can touch. Reduced-size recovery lowers per-basket risk but keeps trading during a bad regime.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: on $100 a 'portion' makes little sense. Prefer halting after a DD tier over trading on at reduced size, because 0.01 is already the minimum lot and cannot be halved.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: no recovery mode. After the DD halt, restart manually at the base configuration.

findings.mechanism: Validation discipline: walk-forward, event replay, and warnings about parameter fragility
findings.description: Ladder-Dragon's replay engine processes archived events in order without look-ahead, and walk-forward trains 'only on older evidence'. It also checks simulated results against real terminal orders and uses a hard 10 USDT notional canary. martin-binance ships backtesting with Optuna parameter optimisation. passivbot has an optimiser with drawdown-aware objectives. MintyGrid's README warns that 'a slight tweak in the settings can also cause catastrophic failure'. hftbacktest models feed and order latency and queue position, and notes that optimal parameters differ by venue.
findings.evidence: READMEs and docs as cited.
findings.blowup_protection: Grid parameters are notoriously overfit-prone: a config that survives in-sample often blows on the next trend. Out-of-sample validation and stress tests are the guard.
findings.hf_relevance: Our pipeline already uses TPE plus walk-forward. Inference: for M1 and 30-min holding, add (1) a realistic per-session spread model and slippage on time and basket stops, (2) Monte Carlo on spread and slippage, (3) a stress window (e.g. Jan 2015 SNB, 2014-15 trend) as a must-survive test, and (4) a small live canary with fixed 0.01 lots before scaling.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: acceptance rule of max DD < 25% on every walk-forward fold and survival of SNB 15-Jan-2015 with a broker SL in place.

findings.mechanism: Static range grids versus trailing grids (spot-only 'never sell at a loss' designs)
findings.description: OctoBot's Grid Trading Mode defaults to spread 1.5%, increment 0.5% and 20 orders per side (covering 99.25%-89.5% of price). It 'never cancels any orders' and 'never sells at a loss'. With trailing enabled it cancels and recreates the whole grid (possibly with market orders) when price leaves the range. Staggered Orders covers very wide bounds with mirror orders after each fill. 51bitquant's binance_grid_trader uses a fixed upper_price/bottom_price and grid_number. infinity-grid's GridHODL/GridSell/SWING/cDCA place fixed-quote-size buys at fixed % intervals, shift buy orders up as price rises, and cap total exposure with MAX_INVESTMENT.
findings.evidence: Docs and READMEs as cited.
findings.blowup_protection: Only works because these are unleveraged spot bots: the inventory is fully paid for and can be held through any drawdown. Risk is capped by MAX_INVESTMENT, not by stops.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: does not transfer to leveraged FX at $100. 'Never sell at a loss' is exactly the open-ended holding that blew our standard-account configs. The useful transferable piece is infinity-grid's fixed quote size per grid plus the MAX_INVESTMENT cap.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: none for direct use. Treat as a counter-example.

failure_modes.mode: Unbounded averaging with no stop (martingale or flat grid held until it reverts)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Loss grows with both trend length and lot growth, with nothing capping it. MintyGrid states 'MintyGrid does not use stop losses, your entire account balance is at risk'. jumpycalm's cBot has no equity or drawdown protection. Ilan's LotExponent 1.667 makes exposure grow geometrically. This is the same failure our backtest found: open-ended holding blew every $100 standard-account config in a 2014-15 style trend.

failure_modes.mode: Retail cost structure applied to a design whose edge comes from rebates
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: The professional HF grid in hftbacktest is profitable on a 0.005% maker REBATE: 'Without alpha, this relies heavily on rebates combined with short-term mean reversion'. A retail MT5 grid pays spread on every fill. Shorter holding means more fills, so a zero-gross-edge grid bleeds faster. Inference: this is why our unfiltered symmetric grid was negative in every structure.

failure_modes.mode: Averaging into news spikes because only NEW grids are blocked, not adds
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: GoldHedgerPro's own changelog: in v4.01 'the martingale kept averaging into spikes (e.g., FOMC) with zero awareness'. A spike fills every layer within minutes, so the full ladder sits at the worst prices.

failure_modes.mode: Leverage and exposure misjudged (lot caps without notional or equity math)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: passivbot shows that the move to bankruptcy is about 1/wallet_exposure: WE 10 means a 10% move. On $100 EURUSD, 0.01 lot is about WE 11, so the user's v6.12 MaxTotalLots 8.0 is far beyond what a $100 account can survive (inference). PunlieGridEA warns its grid 'should not be used with leverage exceeding 3'.

failure_modes.mode: Stop or risk anchored to the wrong reference
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Freqtrade warns that with DCA 'Stoploss is still calculated from the initial opening price, not averaged price', so the real risk of a laddered position is not what it appears. GridMaster Pro measures drawdown from an OnInit equity snapshot, uses an asymmetric recovery threshold (/200), and sizes risk from DefaultSL rather than the SL actually placed. Guards like these fire too late or never.

failure_modes.mode: Loss-recycling: unstuck and recovery modes that keep re-entering a trend
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: passivbot admits: 'Extreme black-swan events may cause the auto-unstuck mechanism to keep taking losses and re-entering continually.' GoldHedgerPro's recovery mode (5 more baskets at 0.5x after a 10% DD) can still compound losses in a sustained trend.

failure_modes.mode: Trend or breakout against a range grid (with stops, the cost is 'death by small stops' instead)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Every grid source notes trend risk. AS-Grid: 'trending conditions present elevated risk'. Zerith is described as 'vulnerable to sustained trends despite ADX filter'. Orchard's stop-loss grid swaps unlimited drawdown for losses at the stop point. Without an entry edge, the stopped version bleeds slowly instead of blowing up (inference).

failure_modes.mode: Both legs of a hedged two-sided grid loaded at once (whipsaw)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: With simultaneous long and short grids, a whipsaw can leave both sides deep. That doubles margin use, swap and spread while net exposure looks small. AS-Grid needs a dedicated 'both sides >= 0.8 x threshold' emergency reduction with a daily trigger cap. Inference: the user's independent BUY and SELL grids have the same exposure.

failure_modes.mode: Time stop defined from the wrong clock, or adds allowed right up to the deadline
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Hummingbot's DCA time limit counts from executor creation, not first fill. Inference: if the clock starts at the wrong event, or new layers are added minutes before the forced close, the time stop crystallises full-ladder losses at the worst point.

failure_modes.mode: Overfit or fragile parameters and opaque code
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: MintyGrid: 'a slight tweak in the settings can also cause catastrophic failure'. The Ilan source is decompiled (gd_ variables), and sonidelav's GridEA hides its logic in a library with no SL or equity guard. You cannot reason about tail risk you cannot read.

failure_modes.mode: No broker-side protection: an EA or VPS outage during a spike
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Basket stops that live only in EA logic do nothing while the terminal is down. Blessing (UsePowerOutSL, POSLPips 600) and GoldHedgerPro (500-pip emergency SL on every position, 'protects if EA crashes') add exchange-side stops for this reason. Ladder-Dragon requires 'verified exchange-side SELL protection' for every filled buy.

notes:
I read about 30 distinct repositories and docs, all read-only via WebFetch on github.com / raw.githubusercontent.com plus GitHub search. Nothing was cloned and no code was copied.

**Access limits**
- hummingbot.org, binance.com, okx.com and mql5.com were blocked by the egress proxy, so the Hummingbot docs pages, the Binance/OKX grid-bot FAQs and the mql5.com articles (e.g. articles/21833 on why grid EAs fail) could not be read.
- For Hummingbot I read the source code on GitHub instead.
- Binance/OKX appear only in search-result snippets, so they are left out of sources_read and not cited.
- The GitHub MCP file reader only allows the user's own repo, so I used WebFetch on raw URLs.

**Accuracy of the summaries**
- WebFetch passes each page through a small summarising model. Formulas and defaults quoted here are as that model reported them from the code. Check the critical numbers in source before relying on them, for example Avellaneda's exact sigma term and the AS-Grid threshold formulas.
- One inconsistency I fixed: for hftbacktest's skew I trust the formula (bid_depth = half_spread + skew*pos/qty, i.e. a long position pushes bids away) over the summariser's prose.
- Every "Inference:" in hf_relevance and parameter_hints is my own reasoning for EURUSD M1/M5 on a $100 account, not a claim from a source.

**Engineering quality**
- Well engineered: Hummingbot v2 executors (triple barrier, activation bounds, DCA executor), passivbot v8 (exposure limits, enforcers, unstuck with a loss allowance, hard stop with cooldown), hftbacktest (latency and queue modelling, honest about rebates), martin-binance (fee-aware TP, budget-normalised martingale, Bollinger/ATR depth, ADX plus Mann-Kendall start gate), GoldHedgerPro v4 (news freezes adds, ATR settle, session profiles, layered equity guards), Freqtrade protections.
- Mid quality: Zerith, Ghost Grid Eye, Blessing 3, AS-Grid.
- Naive or risky: MintyGrid, jumpycalm, sonidelav GridEA, Ilan 1.4 (decompiled), arbitrage-grid-bot (labelled stat-arb but is MA plus additive grid), GridMaster Pro (anchoring and lot-risk bugs), Xtley "HF Grid" (actually a spread-scaled breakout with pending stops, not a grid).

**What this means for the user's EA (inference)**
1. Make the ladder depth the binding constraint, set from a fixed basket risk budget: about 3-5% of $100, i.e. roughly 4 layers of 0.01 at 3-5 pip spacing with a basket stop just past the last layer.
2. Add a hard 30-minute basket time stop counted from the first fill, a TP that decays to break-even plus costs, and a break-even exit at depth.
3. Replace "open both grids every bar" with a stretch-and-reclaim entry plus an M5/M15 trend gate.
4. Floor spacing and TP by spread (raw-spread account strongly preferred).
5. Use net-inventory skew between the BUY and SELL grids.
6. Add cooldowns after losses, a daily loss limit and an equity-peak halt, and broker-side catastrophic stops.
7. Keep the news filter and also freeze adds during news, resuming on an ATR settle.

The hftbacktest result is the key caveat: a professional HF grid's edge is rebates plus mean reversion. On a retail spread account the entry signal has to supply real alpha, or more frequent trading just means paying more spread.

findings.mechanism: Finite, restartable grid cycles with an ex-ante hard stop for the whole grid
findings.description: Treat each grid as a cycle that must end flat: either at the shared TP or at a pre-computed worst-case basket loss. Never let a grid stay open with an unbounded loss. After the cycle closes, restart from scratch with fresh state.
findings.blowup_protection: Turns an unbounded, path-dependent loss into a bounded per-cycle loss. Taranto's result (as summarised) is that a grid with no constraint is ruined with probability 1. Finite cycles with a regime gate are what make positive expectancy possible. The hard stop sets the size of the worst cycle, so ruin needs many consecutive worst cycles, not one trend.
findings.evidence: MQL5 article 21833 (summarised in search results): the grid trading problem is a semimartingale that can have positive expectancy, but 'unconstrained operation leads to almost sure ruin'. 'Finite, restartable cycles with regime-aware gating prevent ruin.' Grid loss after 10 adverse levels is 55 units, against 1,024 for martingale doubling. Taranto: 'the ability to close down some or all trades when the system is in profit and then start the grid system again forms a favorable positive cash-flow cycle'. MQL5 forum summary: 'when the stop loss is the entire deposit, it's a recipe for disaster... a hard stop for the entire grid is just as mandatory as it is for a single trade.'
findings.hf_relevance: The 30-minute maximum hold is the cycle boundary. Every cycle must end flat by T_max. Compute the basket stop in dollars before the first fill, from the ladder (lots x distance), so it is known and fixed rather than discovered live. The current EA has only an optional float-% basket stop and an open-ended hold. Our own backtest found that open-ended holding blew every $100 config, which agrees with the 'ruin with probability 1' result.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: worst-case cycle loss (all layers filled, plus X pips beyond the last fill, plus costs) should be at most 2-4% of equity on $100. Example: 4 layers of 0.01/0.01/0.02/0.02, 4-pip spacing, stop 4 pips beyond the last fill. That is 0.52 lot-pips = $5.2, plus about $0.5 costs, about 5.7% of $100. This is already at the upper limit, so 4 layers is about the maximum depth on a $100 standard account.

findings.mechanism: Time-decaying take-profit schedule plus a forced exit at N minutes
findings.description: The required profit to close falls as the position ages: full TP when young, a smaller TP later, breakeven after that, and a forced market close at a hard time limit whatever the P&L. Freqtrade's minimal_roi is the practitioner reference: {0: 4%, 20 min: 2%, 30 min: 1%, 40 min: 0%}. A value of -1 forces an exit after N minutes. Hummingbot market-making quotes have a max_order_age (default 1800 s = 30 min) after which they are replaced whatever their price.
findings.blowup_protection: Loss is bounded by the distribution of 30-minute adverse excursions, not by the length of a trend. A 2014-15 style multi-month trend can only cost a sequence of capped 30-minute losses, not one compounding basket.
findings.evidence: Freqtrade configuration.md (read in full) quotes the minimal_roi example and the '"<N>": -1' forced-exit semantics. The Hummingbot Avellaneda config (read in full) gives max_order_age as 'A given order's maximum lifetime irrespective of spread' with default 1800 s. The MQL5 forum 182144 summary describes closing all positions after X hours when a minimum profit is met.
