Freqtrade strategy-callbacks.md shows time-stepped stop tightening at 60 and 120 minutes, and says long trades with many position adjustments 'should be closed at regular intervals'.
findings.hf_relevance: This is the mechanism the user's 1-30 minute requirement calls for. It fits the existing shared-TP design: TP_pips(t) is recomputed every tick from the time since the oldest open layer, and SetTP updates the shared TP of that grid only. Also add a no-new-layers cutoff (for example, no adds after minute 15-20) so late layers are not opened just before a forced exit.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference, starting points to optimise: t<5 min: TP = k x ATR(M1,14) (k about 1.0-1.5) or the fixed 2.5-4 pips. 5-15 min: 0.5 x TP. 15-25 min: breakeven + round-trip cost. 25-30 min (T_max): market close. Layer-add cutoff at 15-20 min.

findings.mechanism: Partial 'unstuck' closes of the worst/oldest layer, funded by an explicit realised-loss allowance against peak balance
findings.description: Passivbot does not flatten a stuck grid all at once. It closes a small slice of the position at a loss when price bounces to an EMA band, then uses the freed exposure to re-enter at normal grid prices, which pulls the average entry toward market. All unstuck losses are drawn from a budget: loss_floor = balance_peak x (1 - loss_allowance_pct x total_wallet_exposure_limit). Once the budget is used up, no further unstucking happens until profits rebuild it.
findings.blowup_protection: Losses are realised gradually and in small sizes, and the total is hard-capped relative to peak balance, so the account cannot be bled below a known floor by recovery attempts.
findings.evidence: Passivbot configuration.md and risk_management.md (read in full): unstuck_threshold (exposure ratio eligibility), unstuck_close_pct, unstuck_loss_allowance_pct, and unstuck_ema_dist (long positions close only after price reaches upper_EMA_band x (1+dist)). Quoted: 'Closes a small portion of the bag to reduce exposure... uses the freed-up exposure to buy back in at normal re-entry price.' The docs warn that minimum order size can make a single close exceed the remaining allowance.
findings.hf_relevance: This maps directly onto a per-position 30-minute limit. In a BUY grid during a decline, the oldest layer is also the most underwater and the smallest (flat BaseLot). Time-stopping it first (FIFO) realises a small loss and lets the existing live-position VWAP-TP recomputation lower the shared TP. Tie it to a daily loss allowance so FIFO time-stops cannot grind the account down on a trend day.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: daily unstuck/time-stop loss allowance of 3-5% of the day's peak equity. When exhausted, flatten everything and stop for the day. Prefer the FIFO close on a pullback (price within 0.3-0.5 ATR of the M5 EMA) when there is time left, and as market at T_max otherwise.

findings.mechanism: Exposure cap measured as notional/equity (wallet exposure), not as lots or margin
findings.description: Passivbot measures risk as wallet_exposure = position_size x avg_entry / unleveraged balance, and refuses any entry beyond a wallet exposure limit (WEL). It says explicitly that exchange leverage is irrelevant to risk, and maps exposure to the price move that bankrupts the account: exposure 2 = 50% move, 3 = about 33%, 10 = 10%.
findings.blowup_protection: The account cannot hold more inventory than the ruin-distance math allows, however attractive the next grid level looks. When the cap is reached the grid stops adding and becomes 'stuck' rather than levering up.
findings.evidence: Passivbot risk_management.md (read in full) gives the formula, the 'Passivbot ignores exchange leverage settings...' quote, and the exposure-to-ruin table.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference, applying the formula to the user's case: on $100, 0.01 EURUSD (about $1,150 notional) is already a wallet exposure of about 11. The v6.12 MaxTotalLots of 8.0 (designed for a much larger account) is irrelevant here. At 0.09 lots total ($0.90/pip), a 111-pip move wipes $100. The binding constraint is total lots x distance to the hard stop, so replace MaxTotalLots with a dollar-risk cap.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: on $100, cap total open volume per grid at about 0.04-0.06 lots and both grids' net at 0.06. Better, cap 'lots x pips to hard stop x $10' at 4% of equity. If you need finer granularity, use a cent account.

findings.mechanism: Practitioner equity-per-lot rules and dollar-budget ladder sizing for small accounts
findings.description: Long-running grid users size by equity. Search summaries give 0.01 lot per $500-1,000 as the conservative rule, and 0.01 per $100-200 only on cent accounts for burn-in with capped concurrent orders. One prop-firm guide sizes each level from the loss budget: max lot per level = (daily loss limit x 0.8) / grid span in pips.
findings.blowup_protection: Keeps the full ladder's worst floating loss inside a fixed fraction of equity, so a full-depth adverse sweep is survivable.
findings.evidence: goldbuytrader cent burn-in (search summary): a fixed 0.01-lot test from $100 had a worst floating DD of 45.8% of equity early on, and a worst floating loss of about $132-142 at 0.01 fixed. The vendor recommends a $500 minimum and $1,000 ideal. MQL5 blog 768763 (summary): 'use 0.01 lots for every $500-$1,000', and 'any EA can show 2% drawdown if it trades 0.01 lots on a $10,000 account'. jptradingcapital (summary): the per-level formula above. Exness cent help page (summary): a $100 deposit shows as 10,000 cents.
findings.hf_relevance: The user's plan to start at 0.01 and scale up per layer on $100 standard is about 5-10x more aggressive than the conservative practitioner rules. With a hard 30-minute exit, the ladder only has to survive 30-minute excursions, not multi-day trends, so a denser rule than 0.01 per $500 is defensible. That is only true if the dollar-budget formula is respected.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: lot_per_level = floor_to_step( (0.04 x equity) / (sum over layers of (distance from layer fill to hard stop in pips) x $10 per lot-pip) ). On $100 standard this rounds to 0.01 flat for 3-4 layers. Use a cent account if you want progressive increments.

findings.mechanism: Linear ('soft martingale') or flat lot progression with few adds, never geometric
findings.description: Replace doubling with linear increments and cap the number of adds. Freqtrade's documented DCA example allows only 3 extra entries, with stake multipliers of 1.25x, 1.5x and 1.75x. The stop stays anchored to the original entry price, not to the averaged price.
findings.blowup_protection: Total volume grows roughly quadratically in depth instead of exponentially (55 vs 1,024 units at 10 levels per Taranto). Anchoring the stop to the first entry means averaging cannot quietly widen the risk.
findings.evidence: MDPI Algorithms 19(6):442 (summary): EURUSD H1, 12-month out-of-sample: 444 trades, 65.77% win rate, PF 2.85, 442.6% annual return. Even with linear multipliers, max equity DD was 79.97% against max balance DD of 13.98% (DDR 5.72x). The authors say ML 'does not eliminate the catastrophic-drawdown mechanism'. Ilan (summaries): too large a martingale factor reaches 'critical volume very quickly'. An Ilan 8.0 real-account forward test showed 88% DD. Freqtrade strategy-callbacks.md (read in full) contains the DCA example and the anchored-stop note.
findings.hf_relevance: The user's ladder is already linear (+LotIncrement), which is right. But the MDPI result shows a linear ladder alone still gives about 80% equity DD. It has to be combined with the hard cycle stop and the time exit. On $100 the increment is effectively forced to be either 0 or 0.01 every 2 layers.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: 0.01, 0.01, 0.02, 0.02 (max 4 layers), or flat 0.01 x 5. Never more than 3-4 adds inside one 30-minute cycle. Hard stop anchored to a fixed number of pips from the FIRST fill, not from the VWAP.

findings.mechanism: Volatility-scaled spacing that widens as exposure grows
findings.description: Set the grid step from current volatility rather than as fixed pips, and make each deeper step wider. Taranto/Khan: expected profit is maximised when the grid interval matches the characteristic oscillation amplitude. Passivbot multiplies its re-entry threshold by both wallet-exposure and volatility weights. Its volatility measure is an EMA of ln(high/low) on 1m and 1h candles. The BGC Grid EA recalculates spacing from daily ATR.
findings.blowup_protection: Fewer layers fill during an expanding-volatility impulse, and deeper layers need a larger move to trigger. The ladder therefore spends its depth only on oscillations it can mean-revert, not on the first leg of a trend.
findings.evidence: Passivbot configuration.md (read in full): entry_threshold_base_pct is 'Modified by wallet exposure and volatility weights multiplicatively', and volatility_ema_span_1m/1h is an 'EMA of per-candle log range ln(high/low)'. The Taranto summaries cover interval calibration to oscillation amplitude. The BGC Grid EA summary describes ATR-dynamic spacing and a VolatilityGate.
findings.hf_relevance: On M1/M5 EURUSD, fixed 7.5-pip spacing is too wide for 30-minute cycles in quiet hours and too narrow during a data spike. Scale with ATR(M1) or the M1 log-range EMA, and add an exposure multiplier.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: spacing_n = max(cost_floor, k x ATR(M1,14) x (1 + w x n/N)), with k about 1.5-2.5, w about 0.5-1.0, and cost_floor at least 4x round-trip cost (about 3-4 pips on standard, 2.5-3 on ECN).

findings.mechanism: Adaptive cooldown between layer adds (minimum time between fills)
findings.description: After any position-increasing fill, wait before allowing the next add. Passivbot's adaptive cooldown = clamp(base + exposure_ratio x w_exp + adverse_score x w_adv, min, max): it lengthens when exposure is high and price is moving against the position. Hummingbot's filled_order_delay (default 60 s) and Freqtrade's CooldownPeriod do the same at the order/pair level.
findings.blowup_protection: Stops the classic HF-grid death: one 1-3 minute impulse filling the whole ladder before any mean reversion can happen. Spreading adds over time also gives the regime filter and news filter a chance to stop the cycle.
findings.evidence: Passivbot adaptive_entry_cooldown.md (read in full) gives the formula and adverse score = max(0, -signed_unilateralness) for longs. Hummingbot Avellaneda config (read in full): filled_order_delay default 60 s. Freqtrade protections.md (read in full): CooldownPeriod. Freqtrade warns that loose re-entry logic will 're-entry every 5 secs until you either run out of money, hit the max_position_adjustment limit...'.
findings.hf_relevance: The current EA adds as soon as price is one spacing beyond the newest fill, which in M1/tick terms can mean several layers in seconds. A time gate is cheap to add and especially important at 1-30 minute holding.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: base 60 s, plus 60 s x (open_layers/MaxLayers), plus up to 120 s when the M1 move over the last 3-5 bars is against the grid by more than 1.5 ATR. Clamp to 30-300 s.

findings.mechanism: Market-maker inventory skew across the BUY and SELL grids
findings.description: A market maker shifts its quotes against its inventory. Avellaneda-Stoikov (Hummingbot implementation) uses reservation price = mid - q x gamma x volatility x time_left_fraction, plus an optimal spread term. Hummingbot's pure market-making inventory skew scales bid size up and ask size down (bid_adj = 2 - ask_adj) to move inventory back toward target. A price_ceiling/price_floor permits only sells above a level and only buys below it.
findings.blowup_protection: Exposure on the losing side grows more slowly and is shed sooner. The net position (BUY lots - SELL lots) is pushed back toward zero instead of growing one-sidedly during a trend.
findings.evidence: Hummingbot avellaneda_market_making.pyx (read in full): reservation price and optimal spread formulas, with q = normalised inventory deviation. inventory_skew_calculator.pyx (read in full): linear interpolation of the bid/ask ratio. pure_market_making_config_map.py (read in full): inventory_target_base_pct, inventory_range_multiplier, price_ceiling, price_floor, order_level_amount, ping_pong. Note: the canonical A-S formula uses sigma squared; the fetched summary wrote volatility (inference).
findings.hf_relevance: The user's two magic-isolated grids are effectively a two-sided quote with inventory q = BUY lots - SELL lots. Today they are sized independently. Adapted: when q > 0 (BUY grid heavy in a decline), move the BUY shared TP closer, widen BUY add spacing or skip BUY lot increments, and let the SELL grid restart with normal or larger size. Mirror this when q < 0.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: q_norm = (buy_lots - sell_lots) / max_net_lots. BUY TP multiplier = 1 - 0.5 x max(0, q_norm). BUY spacing multiplier = 1 + max(0, q_norm). Hard ban on heavy-side adds when |q_norm| > 0.8. Mirror for the SELL side.

findings.mechanism: Equity hard stop on smoothed peak-to-trough drawdown, with a flatten-and-cooldown restart policy
findings.description: Passivbot's HSL rebuilds equity including unrealised P&L, tracks the running peak, and computes raw DD and its EMA. It panic-closes only when score = min(raw, EMA) exceeds the red threshold, then applies a restart_after_red_policy of 'always' (restart after cooldown) or 'never' (no restart within the lookback). Simpler EAs use a fixed equity circuit breaker: GridMaster Pro defaults to a 5% max equity DD; Nyao Scalper has a 3-12% basket stop plus min-equity and max-DD halts; Grid Scalper MA has a daily DD stop against the start-of-day balance.
findings.blowup_protection: Puts a floor under equity independent of grid logic. Using the min of raw and smoothed DD avoids a one-tick spike flattening a grid that would have recovered (the whipsaw problem). The cooldown stops immediate re-entry into the same regime.
findings.evidence: Passivbot equity_hard_stop_loss.md (read in full): 'Only the current score authorizes panic. Historical threshold crossings do not latch RED.' equity_hard_stop_loss_risks.md (read in full): 'RED is current intent, not a guarantee of a fill' (gaps, unfilled orders). GridMaster Pro README (read in full): 5% default. Nyao README (read in full): basket 3-12% of equity per profile. ForexFactory Ikarus thread (summary): users 'reported difficulty making [the equity hardstop] work and accounts have blown on backtest'.
findings.hf_relevance: Use three layers, all in equity terms: (1) per-cycle hard stop, (2) daily stop against start-of-day equity that flattens and halts until the next session, and (3) peak-to-trough account stop that halts for days or weeks pending review. The existing DD halt only blocks new grids. Make it flatten.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference for $100: per-cycle 3-4%, daily 6-8%, peak-to-trough 20% (halt and re-optimise). Smooth with an EMA of about 2-5 minutes, but always act on raw DD beyond about 1.5x the threshold (gap protection).

findings.mechanism: Loss-streak circuit breaker (own P&L used as a regime detector)
findings.description: Freqtrade's protections stop trading for stop_duration when trade_limit or more stop-losses occur within lookback (StoplossGuard). MaxDrawdown halts when equity-mode DD over a lookback exceeds max_allowed_drawdown. LowProfitPairs locks a pair whose recent profit ratio is below threshold.
findings.blowup_protection: Losing cycles cluster on trend or volatility-expansion days. Pausing after 2-3 capped losses stops a day of repeated capped losses from adding up to account-level ruin.
findings.evidence: Freqtrade protections.md (read in full): 'If trade_limit or more trades resulted in stoploss, trading will stop for stop_duration', plus MaxDrawdown with calculation_mode 'equity' recommended.
findings.hf_relevance: With 30-minute forced exits, a trending London session can produce several time-stop losses in a row. Count both basket-stop and losing time-stop exits.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: 2 losing exits within 3 hours, or 3 within 8 hours, pauses new cycles for 4-12 hours or until the next session. Rolling 24-hour equity DD above 6% halts until the next day.

findings.mechanism: Trend and volatility regime gate for new cycles AND for adds mid-cycle
findings.description: Start, or keep adding to, a grid only while the market is in a mean-reverting, normal-volatility state. Practitioners report that a trend filter decided survival. Common gates: price slope or EMA filter, ADX, ATR relative to its long average (both too high and too low), and 'dead market' blocks.
findings.blowup_protection: Removes the regime that kills grids (sustained one-way movement) before exposure is built. A mid-cycle check stops further adds when the regime flips while a grid is open.
findings.evidence: ForexFactory Ikarus thread (summary): 'Version 4.79 with EMA Trend Filter enabled survived volatile conditions where the 4.77 version blew up with the same settings.' QuantMonitor (summary): enable only when SMA(50) is rising and ATR/Close is below its 100-period average. Nyao README (read in full): dead-market block when ATR/AvgATR < MinVolRatioToTrade. BGC Grid EA (summary): VolatilityGate on the ATR/drift ratio with cooldown. Taranto (summary): regime-aware gating is part of the positive-EV conditions.
findings.hf_relevance: This addresses our backtest finding that the unfiltered symmetric grid has about zero gross edge. On M1/M5 the gate should use a slower context (M15/H1 slope or ADX) to block counter-trend grids, plus fast ATR bands to block spikes and dead tape.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: allow a new cycle when ADX(M15,14) < 20-25, |EMA(M15,50) slope| < c x ATR, and ATR(M5,14)/SMA(ATR(M5,14),288) is in [0.6, 1.6]. Stop adds (and tighten the time-decay schedule) as soon as the gate fails during a cycle.

findings.mechanism: Start cycles only at statistical extremes (directional fade), not symmetric both-side grids every bar
findings.description: Longer-lived commercial grids do not open blindly. Waka Waka opens its first trade near Bollinger Band extremes on mean-reverting crosses (AUDCAD/AUDNZD/NZDCAD, M15). Nyao gates on a signal score. The MDPI HF-grid paper uses an ML filter trained on simulated grid outcomes and gets a 65.77% win rate.
findings.blowup_protection: The first fill already has a mean-reversion edge, so fewer cycles need to go deep. Depth is where all of the tail risk sits.
findings.evidence: Waka Waka (summaries from NYCServers, TradersUnion, Myfxbook community): Bollinger-extreme entries, max 9 trades spaced 35 pips, 70+ consecutive profitable months. Yet the developer account had >40% DD in early 2024, some user accounts were depleted in March 2024, and one recovery took 80+ days. MDPI (summary): 444 out-of-sample trades, z = 6.65, PF 2.85, but 79.97% max equity DD.
findings.hf_relevance: Our backtest found the symmetric grid on EURUSD M1 has no gross edge. Changing from 'open BUY and SELL every new M15 bar' to 'open only the side that fades a stretched move' is the most direct way to create edge. Waka Waka's 2024 losses show that edge alone does not prevent blowups without hard stops.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: open the BUY grid only if price is at least 2 sigma below the M5 20-period mean (or session VWAP) and the regime gate passes; mirror for SELL. Optionally require a reversal M1 candle. Leave both grids on only inside a detected range (for example, the Asian range when the gate passes).

findings.mechanism: Horizon-aware news filter that flattens and blocks adds, not only new grids
findings.description: The news filter must stop adds inside an open grid, and should flatten before the event. Some EAs gate only new baskets with the time/session filter, while 'grid additions, trailing stops, breakeven closes...continue outside trading hours'. That is the same structure as the user's hour filter, which gates NEW grids only.
findings.blowup_protection: News impulses are the fastest way to fill a full ladder and then gap through the basket stop. Being flat into the release removes that path.
findings.evidence: Nyao README (read in full): automatic pause 15-45 minutes before and after high-impact events, and a warning that the Strategy Tester cannot see the news filter, so backtest drawdowns are 'optimistic'. Grid Scalper MA (summary): the time filter restricts only new basket openings. SNB 15 Jan 2015 (summary): EURCHF floor removed, >11% franc appreciation, 'historic dysfunction'. Our own backtest: pausing adds during news materially reduced DD.
findings.hf_relevance: With a 30-minute maximum hold, the filter becomes simple: do not start a cycle if a high-impact event for EUR or USD is within T_max + buffer. If a cycle is open, flatten at T-5 min. Block new cycles until about T+15-30 min, when spreads normalise.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: block new cycles from T-35 to T+20 min, block adds from T-35, force flat at T-5 (high-impact USD/EUR: NFP, CPI, FOMC, ECB). Optionally suspend the whole day for FOMC/ECB/NFP.

findings.mechanism: Session choice with an explicit rollover blackout
findings.description: Night/Asian-session scalpers exploit quiet ranging hours, but practitioners report the rollover window (about 21:00-22:00 bank rollover) is where spreads widen by several pips and slippage spikes. Tester wins become live losses, and the edge does not scale with lot size.
findings.blowup_protection: Prevents spread spikes from triggering adds or stops and keeps costs predictable. The ranging session provides the oscillation the grid needs.
findings.evidence: Night scalper summaries (MQL5 blog 769397, NYCServers Night Hunter Pro, ForexBenchmark SFE): the rollover-window warning, 'trades a clean tester scores as small wins become small losses on a live feed', and 'higher lot sizes will lead to more slippage'. One SFE review: 'nothing but blow-up accounts'. A Myfxbook-verified night scalper made +215% since Oct 2020 with about 30% max DD from $285. Night Owl (ForexRobotNation summary): the biggest drawback is large stop-losses 'which can take up to several months to recover'.
findings.hf_relevance: For EURUSD 1-30 minute cycles: either a quiet-range session (late Asia / pre-London) with tight ATR spacing, or the liquid London/NY window with strict trend gating. Always black out roughly 20:45-23:30 server time and the first minutes of the London and NY opens. Inference: our M1 data can rank sessions by the ratio of 30-minute mean reversion to cost.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: blackout of rollover ±60-90 min, plus the 15 minutes around the 07:00 and 12:30/13:30 UTC opens and data. Choose the session by out-of-sample backtest of mean 30-minute adverse excursion vs TP hit-rate, not by intuition.

findings.mechanism: Cost-aware TP and spacing floor, a live spread guard, and M5 signals over M1
findings.description: On M1, spread plus commission is the dominant cost, so a backtest without realistic costs is 'meaningless'. Practitioners block entries when spread exceeds a fixed or ATR-derived threshold, and report that M5/M15 beat M1 for retail because the cost is the same while the per-bar move is several times larger.
findings.blowup_protection: Mainly protects against slow bleed rather than blowup, but the two are linked. A strategy with negative expectancy after costs needs ever-larger size and depth to show profit, which is what eventually blows the account.
findings.evidence: Nyao README (read in full): 'spread + commission is the dominant cost', and a Max-Spread filter with fixed or ATR-derived thresholds. Chartsnipe / AppTrading summaries: hit rate has to stay above 60% just to pay costs, and M5 and M15 beat M1 for retail accounts. Our backtest: spread and swap made every structure negative.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference arithmetic: a 0.01 single-layer win with a 3-pip TP is $0.30 gross, minus about $0.07 commission and $0.02 spread on ECN, about $0.21 net. Against a full-depth stop of about $5.7, break-even needs about 96.4% of cycles to win. So TP must be several times the cost and depth must stay shallow. A 30-minute exit also avoids swap, which our backtest found to be a drag.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: TP and spacing at least 3-5x round-trip cost. Use an ECN/raw account (about 0.1-0.2 pip + $5-7/lot RT). Block entries when spread > 1.5x the rolling median. Signal on M5, execute on M1/ticks.

findings.mechanism: Judge the system by equity (floating) drawdown and the worst cycle, not by balance DD or win rate
findings.description: Grid systems report low balance drawdown because losses are 'absorbed through additional positions rather than stop-loss exits'. The MDPI paper formalises this as the Drawdown Dichotomy Ratio = max equity DD / max balance DD. A low drawdown on a tracked account can just reflect tiny lots.
findings.blowup_protection: Prevents the false comfort that leads users to increase lots right before the tail event.
findings.evidence: MDPI (summary): DDR 5.72x (79.97% equity vs 13.98% balance). eatested (summary): 'The low DD was always a misleading metric'. MQL5 blog 768763 (summary): 2% DD at 0.01 on $10k means nothing. ForexFactory 'Can a grid trader survive?' (summary): 'you will get a straight line equity curve until you don't'.
findings.hf_relevance: Optimise and walk-forward on max equity DD, worst single-cycle loss, and DDR. Reject configurations with DDR above about 2 once the hard stop and time exit exist (inference: with hard stops, equity DD and balance DD should converge).
findings.parameter_hints: Inference acceptance criteria: worst cycle ≤ 4% of equity, max equity DD ≤ 20%, DDR ≤ 2, and profit factor > 1.2 after costs out of sample in every year 2012-2020, including 2014-15.

findings.mechanism: Live burn-in on a cent account before scaling
findings.description: Practitioners run grids on cent accounts first because they show real slippage, spreads, swaps and execution quirks with tiny money at risk. Several grid EAs blew within weeks live despite good backtests.
findings.blowup_protection: Finds backtest-to-live divergence (fills, spread at rollover, news slippage) while losses are still small.
findings.evidence: goldbuytrader (summary): cent accounts for burn-in, starting at 0.01 per $100-200 cent-equivalent with capped max orders. MQL5 Trend Line GRID review (summary): 'Acc blown after 1 month in real acc, trade results very different from backtest'. Nyao README: the tester cannot simulate the news filter.
findings.hf_relevance: For 1-30 minute cycles, the edge per cycle is a fraction of a pip, so execution quality decides the outcome. A cent account also gives the lot granularity needed to scale per layer, which a $100 standard account lacks.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: at least 4-8 weeks or 300 or more cycles on a cent account with the same broker and server. Compare live per-cycle P&L and slippage with the simulator before moving to standard.

findings.mechanism: Equity-proportional base lot plus profit extraction above a high-water mark
findings.description: Taranto-based work says the next cycle's base lot should reflect account size, compounding after profitable cycles. Ilan users report that withdrawing profits regularly instead of compounding into the deposit helps survival.
findings.blowup_protection: Risk per cycle stays a constant fraction of equity, and extraction keeps banked profit out of the next tail event.
findings.evidence: MQL5 article 21833 (summary): 'when a cycle ends profitably, the next cycle's base lot should reflect the larger account'. Ilan/LiteFinance (summary): 'if you withdraw profits regularly without increasing the deposit, you can trade more successfully'.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: on $100 the lot step (0.01) limits proportional sizing until about $200-300 on standard, which is another reason to use cent accounts. Recompute the ladder from equity at each cycle start, never mid-cycle.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: base_lot = floor_step(equity / E0) with E0 set by the dollar-budget formula. Sweep 50% of profits above the high-water mark weekly.

findings.mechanism: Manual or scheduled kill switch: grids are run, not left set-and-forget
findings.description: The longest-surviving practitioners treat the grid as a tool they switch off, not an autonomous system. One Blessing user says that since 2013 their account repeatedly blew up while optimising, and that they now use the EA only as an assistant to clear positions after reading the chart.
findings.blowup_protection: A human or calendar-based veto covers regimes the automated filters cannot see (central-bank regime shifts, pegs, war or crisis weeks).
findings.evidence: ForexFactory Blessing 3.9.6 thread (summary): one trader blown on 5 accounts with cumulative losses over 5,000. Blessing could run 12 levels but 'rarely goes past 7... most of the time trades 4 to 5'. Coinmonks/Elitecurrensea/NYCServers grid guides (summary): 'The best grid traders know when to turn the bot on and... when to turn it off'. MQL5 forum (summary): 'Both types of grid systems will wipe your account if you use them as set and forget'.
findings.hf_relevance: Inference: add an input-driven 'trade allowed' calendar (FOMC/ECB/NFP weeks, month-end, holidays) and a remote kill switch. Review after every daily stop.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: maintain a manual blackout date list, and auto-disable after any peak-to-trough DD above 20% until it is manually re-armed.

failure_modes.mode: Sustained one-way move with no retracement, often with no news
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: The grid keeps adding against the move. Floating loss grows roughly with depth squared until margin or equity runs out. Accounts show months of straight-line profit and then die in days. Example from search summaries: a $5,000 account was blown on 19 Oct 2017 by a 150+ pip move without retracement and without major news. SWB grid can 'make over 100% in one month' and then 'wipes out accounts easily' in trending markets. Our own backtest found that open-ended holding blew every $100 config on a 2014-15 style trend.

failure_modes.mode: Geometric or aggressive lot multipliers (martingale)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Volume reaches 'critical' size after a few levels, so a small further move wipes the account at once. 10 levels cost 1,024 units under doubling against 55 for a flat grid. An Ilan 8.0 real-account forward test reached 88% DD. Even a linear 'soft martingale' with an ML entry filter had a 79.97% max equity DD in the MDPI study.

failure_modes.mode: No grid-level hard stop ('the stop loss is the entire deposit') or a stop that is hard to make work
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Without a basket stop the deposit is the stop. Badly built equity stops either never fire in time or whipsaw. Ikarus users reported its equity hardstop was hard to make work and accounts blew even in backtest. Passivbot documents that a stop is intent, not a fill: gaps and unfilled orders can push the realised loss past the threshold.

failure_modes.mode: Undercapitalisation (lot size too large for equity)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: On a $100 account a fixed 0.01 lot already produced a 45.8% floating DD in one cent-account test, with worst floating losses of about $132-142 at 0.01. That is more than the whole $100. Vendors set a $500 minimum and $1,000 ideal for the same settings. Inference: on $100 standard, 0.01 lot is a wallet exposure of about 11, so 0.09 lots open is wiped by about a 111-pip move.

failure_modes.mode: News shocks, gaps and flash moves (SNB 2015 type)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Liquidity disappears, the whole ladder fills or gaps through, and stops slip far beyond their level. Brokers may also leave negative balances. Filters that gate only new baskets, while grid adds continue, leave an open grid fully exposed.

failure_modes.mode: Backtest-to-live divergence (spread, commission, slippage, rollover, news not simulated)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Thin-edge HF systems flip negative live. Examples: a Trend Line GRID account 'blown after 1 month in real acc, trade results very different from backtest'. Night scalpers' tester wins become live losses in the rollover window. The MT5 tester cannot see a live news filter, so backtest DD is optimistic. On M1, spread plus commission is the dominant cost.

failure_modes.mode: Misleading metrics: low balance DD and high win rate hide the floating tail
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Users increase size on the strength of a smooth balance curve, while equity DD is 5x or more the balance DD (MDPI: 79.97% vs 13.98%). A 'low DD' on tracked accounts can also simply reflect tiny lots on a large balance.

failure_modes.mode: Regime change on a 'mean-reverting' instrument (set-and-forget)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Even grids built around mean-reverting crosses fail when the regime shifts. The Waka Waka developer account had a >40% DD in early 2024, some users' accounts were depleted in March 2024, and one recovery took 80+ days. That came after 70+ profitable months, with backtest DD up to 95%. A Blessing user blew 5 accounts (cumulative losses over 5,000) while optimising.

failure_modes.mode: Two-sided grid 'stretch': both grids accumulate and neither reaches its TP
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: In choppy expanding volatility, a bi-directional grid can keep adding in both directions without hitting its minimum profit. Flexy Grid users reported -28% DD with max 20 orders as the grid 'stretches' both ways. Inference: this is directly relevant to the user's simultaneous BUY and SELL grids. It is the inventory problem market makers solve with skew.

failure_modes.mode: Rapid re-entry loops: a single impulse fills the whole ladder in seconds
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Loose re-entry logic re-enters every tick or poll cycle ('every 5 secs until you either run out of money, hit the max_position_adjustment limit...'). On M1 grids a 1-3 minute spike fills every layer before any reversion, so full depth is reached at the worst prices.

failure_modes.mode: Large-stop scalpers: small TP, big SL, recovery takes months
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Night/Asian scalpers win small and often but take rare large stops that 'can take up to several months to recover'. Combined with spread spikes at rollover and slippage that grows with lot size, live expectancy collapses. Some products had 'done nothing but blow-up accounts'.

SYNTHESIS FOR THE USER'S EA (inference, not sourced). These are the mechanisms the sources say separate survivors from blowups. Each fits the existing magic-isolated, live-VWAP-TP design:
(a) A 30-minute hard cycle with a time-decaying shared TP (Freqtrade minimal_roi plus Hummingbot max_order_age = 1800 s).
(b) An ex-ante dollar hard stop per cycle anchored to the first fill, plus daily and peak-to-trough equity stops that FLATTEN, not just block new grids (Passivbot HSL, min of raw and EMA DD).
(c) Total risk capped as lots x distance-to-stop in dollars, replacing MaxTotalLots = 8.0. On $100 standard this allows only about 4 layers of 0.01-0.02. Use a cent account to scale per layer.
(d) An adaptive time gap between adds (60-300 s, Passivbot cooldown) and ATR- and exposure-scaled spacing.
(e) Inventory skew between the BUY and SELL grids (Avellaneda/Hummingbot): shorter TP and wider adds on the heavy side.
(f) A regime gate and a directional-extreme entry instead of opening both grids every bar. Our backtest showed about zero gross edge for the symmetric version.
(g) A news filter that blocks adds and flattens, and refuses to start a cycle whose 30-minute horizon contains an event.
(h) A rollover blackout and a cost floor (TP/spacing at least 3-5x round-trip cost; ECN).
(i) Loss-streak circuit breakers (Freqtrade StoplossGuard).
(j) Cent-account live burn-in.

Break-even arithmetic for $100: 3-pip TP at 0.01 is about $0.21 net, against a full 4-layer stop of about $5.7, so roughly 96% of cycles must win. Both the edge filter and the shallow depth are mandatory.

findings.mechanism: Volatility-expansion kill switch (ATR15/ATR1440 ratio + realised-vol percentile) that blocks new grids AND new layer adds
findings.description: Compute a short/long activity ratio (sum of |1-min returns| over the last 15 min divided by the per-minute average over the last 1440 min). When it is in its top tercile (more than about 2.1x), turn the fade grid off. This was the only regime feature in our own test that clearly changed the sign of short-horizon reversal on EURUSD. An institutional mean-reversion kill-switch spec uses the same idea: disable when realised vol is above the 90th percentile of the trailing year for 5 bars. A separate repo's post-mortem shows the opposite mistake: a filter that unintentionally selects FOR volatility expansion 'adversely selected for the exact regime where mean reversion fails'.
findings.blowup_protection: Removes the states where a >1-sd move keeps going. Those states hold the fattest adverse-excursion tails, which a 30-minute time stop would otherwise turn into realised ladder losses.
findings.evidence: Inference (own computation on the project's Oanda EURUSD M1 mid data, 2012 to 2020.05, script regime_scripts/session_tail.py in the scratchpad). Trigger: |30-min move| > 1 sd. 12-16 UTC: next-30-min reversal +0.42 pip when calm vs -0.29 pip when ATR-expanded; adverse-excursion (MAE) p99 50 vs 68 pips. 17-20 UTC: +0.30 vs -0.93 pip; MAE p99 39 vs 70. 21-23 UTC: +0.37 vs -0.66; MAE p99 28.5 vs 92. Liquid hours 07-16 UTC pooled (regime_cond.py): top tercile gives +0.02 pip at 15 min and -0.165 pip at 30 min; P(continuation >10 pips in 30 min) 0.191 vs 0.159. The S014 kill switch reads: 'realised vol > 90th percentile of trailing 1y for 5 consecutive bars (event regime, 2σ moves are real)'. SUPER_TRADEMAN D2: 'a volatility-expansion filter, not a quality filter, that adversely selected for the exact regime where mean reversion fails'.
findings.hf_relevance: Directly applicable on M1. It is cheap to compute in MQL5 from M1 bars or ticks and reacts within minutes, unlike H1/D1 ADX.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: block new grids and layer adds when ATR15m/ATR1440m > 2.0 (or 1-min realised vol > 90th percentile of the trailing 250 days). Re-enable only after 15-30 consecutive minutes below 1.5. If a grid is already open when the ratio trips, freeze adds and tighten the basket time stop (for example to 10 minutes) instead of averaging further.

findings.mechanism: Trend-strength gates (Kaufman Efficiency Ratio, ADX, Choppiness): use as a coarse higher-timeframe 'do not add' switch, not as an edge source
findings.description: Standard definitions. ER = |net change over N| / sum of |1-bar changes| over N (Kaufman). ADX = Wilder-smoothed directional movement normalised by ATR, which quantifies trend strength. CHOP: near 100 means choppy, near 0 means trending. At 15-30 minute horizons on EURUSD these split future reversal only weakly and non-monotonically, and the spread between buckets is smaller than trading costs. A separate MT5 research log found that efficiency ratios, M15 lag-1 autocorrelation, a 4-hour variance ratio, realised vol and trend t-stats could not time good versus bad periods in advance. The practical role is a slow veto, for example 'ADX14 > 30 on M15/H1 for 5 bars means no new grid', as used in an FX mean-reversion kill-switch spec.
findings.blowup_protection: Stops the grid from starting or averaging into an established intraday trend (the 2014-15 style failure). It does not protect against sudden breakouts out of quiet regimes, which is what the volatility-expansion and news filters are for.
findings.evidence: pandas-ta docstrings: ER is 'invented by Perry J. Kaufman... ER = abs_diff / SUM(volatility, length)'. CHOP: 'Values closer to 100 implies the underlying is choppier whereas values closer to 0 implies the underlying is trending'. ADX: 'meant to quantify trend strength'. Inference (own computation, regime_cond.py): ER60 terciles at trigger time give next-30-min reversal of -0.086 / +0.336 / +0.201 pip (non-monotonic). Rolling VR5(240m) terciles: +0.146 / +0.127 / +0.177 pip (no discrimination). EXP-021 (XAUUSD, M1/M15): 'No feature separates good/bad periods (all |t| < 1.7)... The regime can be described after the fact but not timed in advance with these features.' S014: 'ADX_14 > 30 for 5 consecutive bars... Re-enable mechanically after DD recovers 50% AND ADX returns <25.'
findings.hf_relevance: On M1 these indicators are dominated by noise and lag. Compute them on M15/H1 and use them only to block, never to trigger.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: ADX14(M15) > 30 means no new grids (hysteresis: resume below 25). ER(20) on M15 > 0.5 means no new grids. Treat each added filter as a free parameter and keep at most two or three, to avoid filter stacking or overfitting.

findings.mechanism: Variance ratio / Hurst as an offline pair-and-session suitability test, not a minute-by-minute switch
findings.description: The Lo-MacKinlay variance ratio (VR < 1 means negative serial correlation, i.e. mean reversion) is the right statistic for asking whether a session is fadeable. On recent EURUSD 15-minute data it shows weak, borderline-significant mean reversion: VR(16) about 0.92. That magnitude is economically tiny for a retail trader. Hurst via R/S is badly biased in the short windows an EA would use: on a random walk, raw R/S gives about 0.66, and the corrected null is about 0.40-0.43 with a ±0.12 indistinguishable band. One FX repo dropped its Hurst feature because it read H of about 0.88 everywhere. The conclusion is to run VR (heteroskedasticity-robust, debiased) on weeks or months of data per session to decide whether a session is worth gridding, then leave it fixed.
findings.blowup_protection: Prevents false confidence from a noisy real-time 'H < 0.5' reading, which would switch the grid on at random. It also identifies the sessions where returns are least persistent, which bounds the tail of ladder adverse excursion.
findings.evidence: arch VarianceRatio docstring: null 'The process is a random walk'; 'Rejection of the null with a positive test statistic indicates the presence of positive serial correlation'; robust and debiased options default to True. nadav2 robustness.json, EURUSD 15-min bars (Dukascopy, 2025-01 to 2026-02): VR(2)=0.979 (p=0.083), VR(4)=0.957 (p=0.049), VR(8)=0.949 (p=0.112), VR(16)=0.920 (p=0.075); GBPUSD VR(16)=0.916 (p=0.031); USDJPY around 1. markets.json: EURUSD 15m lag-1 autocorrelation -0.0207. Anaji00 quant_calc.py: 'the raw slope puts a genuine random walk near 0.66'; 'median between 0.40 and 0.43'; RANDOM_WALK band ±0.12. rellis3 lesson: 'R/S is biased toward finding H > 0.5 in small samples'; featureHurst dropped, 'no usable predictive relationship', H about 0.88 across instruments. nolds: Anis-Lloyd-Peters correction is available.
findings.hf_relevance: VR at q = 2-16 on 1-5 minute bars matches the 1-30 minute holding horizon. With lag-1 autocorrelation of about -0.02 at 15 minutes, the expected snap-back after a 10-pip move is about 0.2 pip (inference), well below spread plus commission.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: per session block, compute robust debiased VR(q) for q in {5, 15, 30} on 1-min mid returns over a rolling 60-120 trading days. Enable the grid in a block only if VR(15) < 0.95 with z < -2. Do not compute Hurst on fewer than about 500-1000 points, and if you do, test against the corrected null of 0.43, not 0.5.

findings.mechanism: Session selection: grid only the quiet Asian block after spreads normalise; hard no-trade 19:00-23:00 UTC (rollover); be flat before the daily reset
findings.description: Fade-friendly behaviour is strongest and tails are thinnest in the Asian block, which is also where volatility is lowest. The rollover and Asia-handover window looks great in mid-price backtests but is untradeable because live spreads there are many times the gross edge. A live Saxo measurement shows EURUSD median spread 1.1 pip from 00:00 to 18:00 UTC, maxima up to 18 pips at 19:00-20:00, median 2.7 at 21:00, and normal again by 22:00. A minute-bar FX mean-reversion study found 47.9% of its gross PnL in 21:00-02:00 UTC, needing 0.90 pip round-trip to break even there, and noted that 'retail rollover spreads on EURUSD are multiples of' that.
findings.blowup_protection: Avoids the hours where spread spikes alone can turn a basket TP into a loss and where stop-hunting wicks hit an averaging ladder. It also makes swap exposure zero when combined with the 30-minute cap.
findings.evidence: sentinel M10b_SPIKE (Saxo live, 2026-06-15 to 08-21): 'EURUSD median is 1.1 pips in every hour from 00:00 to 19:00 UTC'; 19:00 max 9.9; 20:00 median 1.5 / max 18.3; 21:00 (rollover) median 2.7 / max 11.2; 22:00 median 1.3 / max 1.5. It recommends widening the rollover exclusion to 19:00-21:00 UTC or using a live spread threshold. fx_hermes B02: 21:00-02:00 UTC = 47.9% of gross PnL; breakeven cost per bucket (2022) rollover/Asia 0.90, LDN/NY overlap 0.64, London 0.31 pip round-trip. mt5kit defines the rollover window as 21:45-22:30 UTC and classes EURUSD as 'Day-Only'. Inference (own, session_tail.py): Asia 00-06 UTC sd30 = 6.0 pips, reversal +0.40 pip, MAE p99 32 pips; overlap 12-16 UTC sd30 = 12.4, reversal +0.15, MAE p99 58.
findings.hf_relevance: The user's hour filter currently gates only NEW grids. For a 1-30 minute scalper, the session end must also force-flatten and freeze adds.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: allowed new-grid window about 00:30-06:00 UTC (optionally 08:30-11:30 UTC if calm per the ATR ratio). No new grids 19:00-23:59 UTC, force flat by 20:45 UTC, and no layer adds within 30 minutes of the window end. Also gate on live spread <= 1.3x its rolling 60-minute median.

findings.mechanism: London-open opening-range breakout veto: no fade grid from 07:00 to about 08:30 UTC, or none once the Asian range has broken
findings.description: The London open is the classic opening-range breakout time for FX: the Tokyo range sets thresholds and London breaks them. Fading that first break with an averaging grid exposes the ladder to a heavy tail of extension. Average follow-through is small, so this is a risk veto, not a signal. Intraday momentum, where the first window predicts the last, is documented in FX (Elaut, Frömmel and Lampaert 2018, on RUB/USD only, as relayed by a secondary catalog).
findings.blowup_protection: Removes the single most common daily trigger for a one-way ladder fill in the first hour of London.
findings.evidence: Inference (own, orb.py on Oanda M1 mid): 1,998 weekdays with a first break of the 00:00-06:59 UTC range during 07:00-10:59 UTC; median Asian range 26.8 pips. Max extension beyond the break level within 60 minutes: p50 9.1, p90 26.2, p99 55.6 pips. Mean follow-through +1.05 pip at 30 minutes and +0.42 at 60 minutes. je-suis-tm README: 'Tokyo FX trading hour is GMT 0:00 a.m. - GMT 8:59am. London FX trading hour begins at GMT 8:00 a.m.', with an 'abnormal volatility limit' to skip erratic opens. Catalog: Elaut-Frömmel-Lampaert 2018 'First 30 minutes predict last 30 minutes', and the Adjei Rounce 2025 Asia-range London-break study (unverified, secondary).
findings.hf_relevance: Directly sets the session clock for an M1/M5 grid.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: no new grids 06:45-08:30 UTC. After 08:30, allow grids only if price is back inside the Asian range or the ATR ratio is < 1.5. Never place the deepest layers just beyond the Asian high or low.

findings.mechanism: Scheduled-flow stand-aside calendar: macro releases, ECB/WMR fixes, NY option cut, month-end
findings.description: Beyond the economic calendar, FX has recurring flow events with documented volatility and order-flow effects: the 4pm London WMR fix (extreme volatility, worst at month-end), the ECB reference rate at 14:15 CET, and the NY 10:00 option cut. Around US data, conditional-mean jumps occur. A secondary review relays these windows from Andersen et al. (2003), Evans (2018), Krohn et al. (2024) and Ito-Hashimoto (2006). Prop-firm rules encode similar windows: FTMO ±2 minutes, FundingPips ±5 minutes for releases and ±10 minutes for speeches.
findings.blowup_protection: A grid with no per-position stop is most exposed to jump risk. Flattening and freezing adds around scheduled jumps removes the gap-through-all-layers scenario.
findings.evidence: RT3_MICROSTRUCTURE table: US data 8:30 ET '14:30 ± 15 min' hard stand-aside (Andersen et al. 2003 AER); ECB fix '14:15 ± 10 min' ('~2.5bp USD pre-fix drift then revert', Krohn et al. 2024); NY cut '16:00 ± 10 min' CET; WMR fix '17:00 ± 5 min' CET hard, 'Extreme volatility & negative autocorr... month-end worst' (Evans 2018). FTMO: '2 minutes before and ending 2 minutes after'. FundingPips: '5 minutes before the news or 5 minutes after', speeches 10/10.
findings.hf_relevance: At 1-30 minute holding, a ±15/30 minute window around tier-1 releases removes only a few percent of trading time but most jump exposure. Our own backtests already showed that pausing adds during news cut drawdowns.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: tier-1 releases (NFP, CPI, FOMC, ECB): no new grids from 30 minutes before to 30 minutes after, plus force-flatten 5 minutes before. Fixes: WMR 15:55-16:10 London time (double-weight at month-end), ECB 13:05-13:25 UTC. Test the calendar from a CSV in the tester, because MQL5 calendar functions are empty there (see backtest finding).

findings.mechanism: Round-number / stop-cluster aware layer placement and add-pause after a level break
findings.description: Osler's dealer-order data shows take-profit orders clustering AT round numbers (00/50), which tends to reflect price, and stop-loss orders clustering JUST BEYOND them, which accelerates price once crossed. A fade grid whose deeper layers sit just past a round number is buying into the stop cascade. A more robust ladder anchors layers on the near side of round levels and pauses adds for a few minutes after a clean break.
findings.blowup_protection: Lowers the chance that several layers fill in one stop-run burst, where the post-crossing move is larger and longer-lasting.
findings.evidence: RT3_MICROSTRUCTURE summarising Osler (2003, JF; EUR/USD orders Aug 1999-Apr 2000, about 9,700 orders, more than $55bn): 'Take-profit orders cluster at round numbers'; 'stop-loss orders cluster just beyond round numbers'. Osler (2005): USD/DEM 'moved 0.061% in 15 min post-crossing vs 0.054% post-arbitrary number (p<0.001)', and the effect 'persists for ~hours'. Cited caveat: the mean excess is small (about 0.7bp in 15 min) and concentrated in tail cascades.
findings.hf_relevance: The 15-minute post-crossing horizon matches the holding window. This is a tail-risk adjustment, not an edge.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: if a candidate layer price lies within 2 pips beyond a 00/50 level in the adverse direction, either move it to the far side by 3-4 pips or skip it. After price closes an M1 bar more than 3 pips through a 00 level against the grid, pause adds for 5-10 minutes.

findings.mechanism: Volatility- and exposure-scaled spacing and TP (passivbot V8 / Avellaneda-style), instead of a fixed 7.5-pip spacing
findings.description: Production grid bots widen re-entry distance with both volatility and current exposure. passivbot V8: effective_threshold = threshold_base × max(1, 1 + we_ratio×we_weight + vol_1h×w1h + vol_1m×w1m), where volatility is 'the EMA of per-candle log range ln(high/low)' and we_ratio = wallet exposure / limit. The close threshold widens additively. Hummingbot's grid executor exposes min_spread_between_orders, max_open_orders, order_frequency, a whole-grid stop-out limit_price and a triple barrier. Its Avellaneda MM recomputes spreads every order_refresh_time from a tick volatility buffer. A fixed pip spacing means very different risk across sessions, because 30-minute sd varies 2.6x.
findings.blowup_protection: As the ladder deepens or volatility rises, layers get further apart, so a fixed total adverse move fills fewer, smaller layers. That caps the lot-weighted exposure a trend can force onto the account.
findings.evidence: passivbot configuration.md quotes above. Hummingbot GridExecutorConfig: limit_price 'Stop-out price for the whole grid, beyond the losing edge', max_open_orders=5, min_spread_between_orders=0.0005, triple_barrier_config. Avellaneda config: volatility_buffer_size default 200 ticks, order_refresh_time. Inference (own): sd of 30-minute moves by block: Asia 6.0, London 9.7, overlap 12.4, NY pm 8.1, rollover 4.7 pips, so a 7.5-pip spacing is about 1.25 sd in Asia but 0.6 sd in the overlap.
findings.hf_relevance: Use M1 log-range EMA (vol_1m) plus M60 (vol_1h) exactly as passivbot does. It is computable in OnTimer every 5-15 seconds.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: spacing_k = max(3 × all-in round-trip cost, c × σ15(session EWMA)) × (1 + 0.5 × lots_open/MaxTotalLots), with c about 1.0-1.5. Basket TP distance about 0.5-0.8 × current spacing but at least 4x all-in cost. Cap layers at 3-4 for a $100 account.

findings.mechanism: Hard triple barrier per basket (TP / basket stop / time limit) sized from the p99 30-minute adverse excursion
findings.description: Institutional executors attach three barriers to every position: stop_loss, take_profit and time_limit. Hummingbot's grid executor adds a whole-grid stop-out price. For a 1-30 minute grid, the time limit converts tail risk into realised loss, so ladder depth × lots must be sized so that a p99 adverse excursion inside 30 minutes costs a small fraction of equity. On EURUSD that excursion is 30-60+ pips depending on session.
findings.blowup_protection: Puts a hard bound on loss per basket. Without it, open-ended holding blew every $100 configuration in our backtests.
findings.evidence: Hummingbot TripleBarrierConfig fields stop_loss, take_profit, time_limit; example time_limit=300 ('5 minutes time limit'); GridExecutorConfig.limit_price stop-out. Inference (own, session_tail.py): MAE beyond trigger within 30 minutes, p95/p99: Asia 18.0/32.4, London AM 26.2/43.3, overlap 34.2/58.2, NY pm 25.5/47.6 pips. Inference (arithmetic): 6 layers at 5-pip spacing with lots 0.01..0.06 = 0.21 lots with average entry 16.7 pips below the first. A 50-pip move then loses about $70, i.e. 70% of $100. 3 layers at 8 pips with 0.01/0.02/0.03 = 0.06 lots lose about $24 on the same move.
findings.hf_relevance: This is the core of the user's 1-30 minute requirement. The time barrier should apply to the basket's first entry time, not to each layer.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: basket time limit 20-30 minutes from the first fill. Basket stop = min(price level at p99 MAE for the session, equity loss of 8-10% of balance). Sizing rule: Σ lots × (MAE_p99 − avg-entry distance) × $10/pip ≤ 0.08 × equity, which on $100 means at most about 0.05-0.06 total lots and 3 layers.

findings.mechanism: Add cooldown plus fill-markout monitoring (adverse-selection detector)
findings.description: Market makers do not re-quote instantly after being filled. Hummingbot's Avellaneda default filled_order_delay is 60 seconds ('The delay before placing a new order after an order fill'). Desks measure markout, the mid-price move after each fill at several horizons: persistent negative markout means you are trading against informed or toxic flow. For a grid, each layer add is a fill into momentum. If the 30-60 second markout of adds is persistently negative, the regime is trending and adds should stop.
findings.blowup_protection: Prevents a burst of adds within one impulsive move, so several layers cannot fill in under a minute, and gives a live, model-free trend detector.
findings.evidence: Hummingbot config: filled_order_delay default 60 s. QuestDB markout: 'Negative markout signals adverse selection — the market moved against you... characteristic of toxic flow'; horizons from 0 to 30 s in 5 s steps, extended to 10 minutes. Alpha Capital (via RoundTrip compliance doc) bans '3 or more positions, each opened within 60 seconds of the previous one... as part of the same trade idea'.
findings.hf_relevance: Implementable in MQL5 by logging mid at fill and at +5 s / +30 s / +60 s / +5 min per layer.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: at least 90-120 seconds between layer adds, and an add requires the latest M1 bar to have closed back in the grid's favour (a 'stall' confirmation). If the median 60-second markout of the last 20 adds is worse than -0.5 × spacing, disable new grids for the rest of the session.

findings.mechanism: Cost-to-edge gate: require gross edge ≥ 2x all-in round-trip cost; pick the cheapest commission account
findings.description: Measured gross mean reversion on EURUSD at 15-30 minutes after a 1-sd move is a few tenths of a pip. All-in costs: raw ECN about 0.0-0.1 pip spread plus $7/lot round-trip (0.7 pip) is about 0.8 pip. Tickmill-style $4/lot is about 0.5 pip. Standard accounts are about 0.8-1.4 pip (a recorded standard-account spread already contains markup, so do not also add commission). One independent minute-bar FX mean-reversion study failed for exactly this reason and adopted a pre-committed kill rule.
findings.blowup_protection: Prevents deploying a structure whose expectancy is negative after costs, which slowly bleeds a $100 account and tempts larger ladders.
findings.evidence: fx_hermes B02: gross edge 0.406 bps/trade; at 0.5 bp/side the result is -0.094 bps; 'Anything whose gross edge is under ~0.5 bps is untradable'; kill rule 'if the best configuration's gross edge is under 2x its assumed round-trip cost in 6 of 8 years, B03 is automatically rejected'. JCAMP broker analysis: IC Markets/Pepperstone '$3.50 per lot per side ($7.00 round-trip)', raw 0.0-0.1; FP Markets $3.00/side; Tickmill $2.00/side. opendocs: 'Commission (Raw Spread) 7 ... per round turn lot'. ahmetcanunaldi EXP-106b: 'recorded Vantage spread (≈ 1.2–1.4 pips) is a standard-account spread that already contains the markup... → double counting'. Inference (own): mean reversal after a 1-sd move +0.15 to +0.40 pip (mid, before costs). S014: 'Cost-to-edge ratio ~0.7-1.5 — frequently broken at retail spread'.
findings.hf_relevance: At 0.01 lot, $7/lot round-trip = $0.07 per round trip = 0.7 pip. Every layer pays it. With 3 layers per basket and 10-20 baskets per day, costs dominate.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: use a raw/ECN account with ≤ $5/lot round-trip. Block trading when live spread plus commission exceeds 1.0 pip. Size TP so that TP ≥ 4 × all-in cost. In optimisation, reject any configuration whose gross edge per trade is < 2 × cost in most years.

findings.mechanism: Per-order live spread re-check relative to a rolling median; respect stop and freeze levels; assume gap fills beyond deviation
findings.description: Spread must be checked immediately before each layer's OrderSend, not once per tick or bar, and judged relative to its own recent distribution. Brokers freeze modifications near TP, and on gaps a market order fills at the next price even beyond the deviation setting, so worst-case loss is distance plus gap. Spread-quality metrics used by MT5 tooling include the P95/median 'stability ratio' and the percentage of time spread is above 1.5x baseline.
findings.blowup_protection: Stops a ladder from adding at blown-out spreads during spikes and avoids failed TP modifications leaving a basket unprotected.
findings.evidence: KARL 04-pitfalls: 'Spread can widen 100x between signal check and OrderSend... re-check SYMBOL_SPREAD immediately before each grid-level OrderSend'; 'broker fills at the next available price even if it exceeds deviation'; 'modify operations rejected' near TP, check SYMBOL_TRADE_FREEZE_LEVEL. mt5kit: 'Stability Ratio... P95 / Median... > 2.0x indicates erratic spreads'; 'Widen (>1.5x)%'.
findings.hf_relevance: Critical at M1, where adds and TPs are a few pips apart.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: allow an add only if spread ≤ min(abs_cap, 1.5 × median spread over the last 60 minutes). abs_cap is about 0.5 pip raw or about 1.6 pip standard. Log the spread at each fill for TCA.

findings.mechanism: Server-request budget: replace the 'modify every position's TP after each add' design with a virtual basket TP plus one server-side disaster stop
findings.description: The EA recomputes one shared TP and modifies every position in the grid after each add. At high frequency this sends many modify requests: with n layers, add k costs about k modifies. Prop and broker risk systems flag request hyperactivity: FTMO cites more than 2,000 server requests per day and 200 orders at a time; The5ers bans excessive server requests and 'bulk trading'. Freeze levels can also reject modifies near TP. A virtual basket TP (close all at market when the bid or ask reaches the computed level), plus a far server-side catastrophic SL per position, cuts requests to about 2 per layer.
findings.blowup_protection: Avoids broker throttling or rejections that could leave some layers without an updated exit, and avoids account-level rule breaches.
findings.evidence: RoundTrip compliance doc (quoting FTMO): 'more than 2,000 server requests per day'; '200 orders at a time and 2000 max positions per day'. The5ers 'excessive number of server requests per day' and 'bulk trading (multiple trades are open simultaneously)'. KARL: modify rejected near TP / freeze level. Inference: request count is from the user's SetTP design as described.
findings.hf_relevance: Matters only at high frequency. At M15 with few grids per day it was harmless.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: keep a basket target in memory, recompute it after every fill, and close all layers with market orders (or close-by on a hedging account) when touched. Keep only a static disaster SL per position at the basket stop level. Rate-limit modifies to ≤ 1 per position per 30 s.

findings.mechanism: Backtest fidelity protocol: real ticks from the target broker, Random delay, commission, CSV news calendar, and a 'rougher model must not look better' red-flag test
findings.description: With TP and spacing of a few pips, the intrabar path decides which of add / TP / stop happens first. MT5 '1 minute OHLC' generates only 4 ticks per M1 bar and invents the intrabar path. 'Every tick based on real ticks' replays recorded bid/ask, so spread varies within a bar, but it silently falls back to generated ticks where real ticks are missing and ignores ticks where M1 is missing. Bar-based engines document the same ambiguity: 'the first visited level determines which order can fill first', and fills at touched limits are assumed. In the tester the MQL5 news calendar (CalendarValueHistory) generally returns nothing, so a calendar-based news filter is absent in backtests. Without Random delay, market orders always fill at the requested price.
findings.blowup_protection: Prevents shipping a configuration whose profitability comes from optimistic intrabar ordering, constant spreads or a news filter that did not run. That is the usual reason a grid that 'never lost' in the tester blows live.
findings.evidence: ThomasPraun / KARL 03: 1-minute OHLC 'Generates only OHLC ticks per M1 bar (4 per bar)'; KARL: 'Without Random Delay, your market order ALWAYS fills at the requested price'. vedkanani validation report (relaying metatrader5.com tick_generation): real ticks 'replays recorded Bid/Ask ticks; spread can change within a minute bar'; 'If M1 exists but real ticks are missing for a minute, MT5 fills with generated ticks'; 'if tick data exists but M1 is missing, the ticks are ignored'. vedkanani master research: 'Results IMPROVING as model gets rougher = timing-sensitive strategy = unreliable. Documented: PF 1.19 (real ticks) → 1.48 (open prices)'. nyao README: 'CalendarValueHistory... generally returns nothing inside the Strategy Tester'. tradermonty: Model=4 needs downloaded broker ticks; a '32 ms' ping-based random delay with no INI key. Nautilus bar-execution: 'The path matters when both a protective stop and a profit target lie inside the same bar'. freqtrade: 'All orders are filled at the requested price (no slippage) as long as the price is within the candle's high/low range'. Inference (own): share of EURUSD M1 bars with range ≥ 3 pips is 0.20 in London AM and 0.28 in the overlap (≥ 5 pips: 0.05 / 0.09), so with 2-5 pip TPs and spacing, same-bar ambiguity is frequent in liquid hours. Our Oanda M1 data is also mid-price, which needs a separate spread model.
findings.hf_relevance: This decides whether any 1-30 minute grid result can be trusted. The Python simulator on M1 mid OHLC should be calibrated against an MT5 real-tick run of the same configuration.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: (1) final validation in MT5 with 'Every tick based on real ticks' on the actual broker's ticks, history quality ≥ 99%, commission set, Random delay on, and the news calendar loaded from a CSV file. (2) Run the same configuration in 1-minute OHLC and real ticks: if PF or net is better in OHLC, treat it as fragile. (3) In the Python simulator, use adverse ordering (stop or add before TP within a bar) and a session-dependent spread profile as the pessimistic bound.

findings.mechanism: Explicit fill / latency / last-look model in research (feed latency, order latency, queue, rejection, slippage probability)
findings.description: HFT-grade backtesters model feed latency, order-entry latency, order-response latency and queue position, and warn against both overly optimistic and overly pessimistic fills. Bar or L1 engines use prob_fill_on_limit and prob_slippage (one tick adverse) knobs. Retail FX liquidity is often last-look: an LP holds the order 1-100 ms and can reject or re-price, and asymmetric rejection shows up as negative millisecond markout. A grid that adds at market during fast moves is exactly the flow most exposed to this.
findings.blowup_protection: Prevents backtests from assuming perfect fills on the adds and exits that matter most (fast adverse moves), which understates basket losses.
findings.evidence: hftbacktest README: 'Backtest accounting for both feed and order latency'; 'Order fill simulation that takes into account the order queue position'; backtesting 'should neither rely on an overly pessimistic approach... nor on an overly optimistic one'. latency_models.rst: feed / order-entry / order-response latency. Nautilus fill-models: 'prob_fill_on_limit controls whether a limit order fills when its price is touched'; 'A successful slippage draw moves the fill one tick against the order direction'. QuestDB last-look: 'typically 1–100ms'; 'asymmetric rejection — accepting trades only when the price has moved in the LP's favor'. ahmetcanunaldi: '0.3 pip slippage/side' assumption on top of commission.
findings.hf_relevance: Model slippage as state-dependent: near zero in calm Asia, 0.2-0.5 pip per side on adds during ATR expansion or news (inference).
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: Python simulator: slippage per side = 0.1 pip × (1 + 2 × max(0, ATRratio − 1)) plus an extra 0.5 pip within ±2 minutes of events. Assume prob_fill_on_limit of about 0.5 for TPs only touched by 0.1 pip. Live: VPS in the same data centre as the broker's MT5 server (ask the broker), and track rejection/requote rates.

findings.mechanism: Live TCA kill switch: halt when realised costs or slippage drift above model
findings.description: Institutional mean-reversion specs include an execution-quality breaker as well as a P&L breaker: disable when cumulative slippage exceeds 1.5x the modelled spread, and when drawdown exceeds a threshold, with mechanical re-enable rules. For a scalping grid with a thin edge, cost drift alone can flip expectancy.
findings.blowup_protection: Catches broker-side degradation (wider spreads, last-look rejections, slippage) before it compounds into a drawdown spiral.
findings.evidence: S014 kill_switch_logic: '(iv) cumulative slippage YTD > 1.5x model spread'; '(i) DD > 15% from peak'; 're-enable mechanically after DD recovers 50%'. QuestDB markout: 'Monitoring counterparty-specific markout curves helps identify which LPs generate toxic flow'. fx_hermes: pre-committed kill criterion of gross edge < 2x cost.
findings.hf_relevance: Rolling 1-2 week windows give hundreds of fills, enough to estimate cost drift quickly at high frequency.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: halt new grids if the rolling 200-fill average (spread + slippage + commission) > 1.5 × model cost, or if the equity drawdown from peak is > 15% on the $100 account. Resume only after a manual review or a 50% recovery.

findings.mechanism: Swap elimination via the hard 30-minute cap plus a session cut-off before the server-day rollover
findings.description: Swap is charged on positions held through the server rollover, with triple swap on Wednesday at IC Markets, whose server time is GMT+2 winter / GMT+3 summer. With a 30-minute hard maximum hold, no new grids in the 60 minutes before server midnight, and force-flat before rollover, swap is structurally zero. That removes one of the two costs that made our symmetric grid negative.
findings.blowup_protection: Removes overnight carry and rollover spread exposure, and the rollover gap and spread spikes, from every basket.
findings.evidence: opendocs (IC Markets specs): swap 'Variable - Triple on Wednesday'; server time 'GMT+3 (summer) / GMT+2 (winter)'; 'Scalping allowed: Yes', 'Hedging allowed: Yes'. Saxo spreads at 19:00-21:00 UTC (see the session finding). Prior project finding: swap made the grid negative.
findings.hf_relevance: This falls out of the user's 1-30 minute requirement automatically, if the cut-off is enforced on adds as well as new grids.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: last new grid at 20:00 UTC, last add at 20:15, force flat at 20:45 UTC (winter; shift by DST relative to the NY-close server clock).

findings.mechanism: Holding-time and frequency design that stays clear of 'tick scalping / HFT / latency arbitrage' rules
findings.description: Retail ECN brokers such as IC Markets allow scalping and hedging, but prop firms and some brokers define and ban tick scalping (durations of seconds), HFT, latency arbitrage, server spamming, bulk simultaneous trades and position clustering. Alpha Capital requires an average trade duration above 2 minutes and at least 50% of profit from trades over 2 minutes. FundedNext Futures flags trades opened and closed within 10 seconds (30% warning, 40% breach). A grid whose individual layers hit 2-3 pip TPs within seconds can fall into these definitions even though the basket is 1-30 minutes.
findings.blowup_protection: Avoids the non-market ruin path of trade cancellation, profit confiscation or account closure, which a $100 grid cannot survive.
findings.evidence: The5ers FAQ: tick scalping = 'entering and exiting positions within seconds'; HFT = 'majority of trade durations span is measured within a few seconds or less'; bans latency arbitrage. RoundTrip compliance doc: Alpha Capital 'average duration of all your trades to be greater than 2 minutes... At least 50% of your gross generated profits must come from trades that exceed 2 minutes'; '3 or more positions, each opened within 60 seconds'; FTMO request limits; Topstep 'average durations measured in seconds, not minutes'. FundedNext rules file: micro-scalping 'opening and closing trades within 10 seconds', 30% warning / 40% breach. opendocs: IC Markets 'Scalping allowed: Yes'.
findings.hf_relevance: Sets a floor on TP distance and add spacing in time. That is also good economics, since sub-minute trades pay full spread for almost no expected move.
findings.parameter_hints: Inference: minimum basket age of 2 minutes before a TP close is allowed (or TP ≥ about 1 sd of a 2-minute move). Average hold target 5-15 minutes. ≤ 2 opens per 60 s. Read your broker's client agreement for 'arbitrage' or 'abusive trading' clauses before going live.

failure_modes.mode: Fading volatility expansion (US session impulse, post-news drift)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: When short-term activity is more than about 2x its daily norm, the sign of EURUSD 30-minute reversal flips: -0.29 pip in 12-16 UTC and -0.93 pip in 17-20 UTC, with MAE p99 of 68-92 pips. A grid with no per-position stop keeps adding into the move, and the 30-minute time stop then realises the deepest loss (inference, own computation).

failure_modes.mode: Mid-price backtest edge concentrated in rollover / Asia handover
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Mean-reversion PnL in mid or average-spread backtests concentrates in 21:00-02:00 UTC (47.9% of gross in one FX M1 study), where live EURUSD spreads are 2.7 pip median and up to 11-18 pip. The live account bleeds on spread, and a basket TP can become a loss.

failure_modes.mode: Gross edge smaller than all-in cost
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Gross short-horizon reversal is about 0.15-0.45 pip per trigger, while all-in cost is about 0.5-1.4 pip per round trip per layer. Expectancy is negative, and the natural response (bigger lot ladders to 'make it work') converts slow bleed into ruin.

failure_modes.mode: Optimistic tester modelling (1-minute OHLC path, constant spread, no delay, news filter silently off)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: With 2-5 pip TPs and spacing, 20-28% of liquid-hour M1 bars span ≥ 3 pips, so invented intrabar paths decide wins. The real-tick mode can silently mix generated ticks. CalendarValueHistory is empty in the tester, so news protection never ran. A configuration that is better in the rougher model (PF 1.19 real ticks vs 1.48 open prices) is timing-fragile and fails live.

failure_modes.mode: Noisy or inert regime filters (Hurst on short windows, thresholds that never bind)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Short-window R/S Hurst reads about 0.66 on a pure random walk (corrected null about 0.43 with a ±0.12 noise band), so 'mean-reverting' readings are random. One repo saw H of about 0.88 everywhere. Another system's trend filter threshold sat above the 99th percentile and blocked only 3.9% of signals. The grid then runs unfiltered while the operator believes it is protected.

failure_modes.mode: Regime features that describe the past but do not time the future
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Efficiency ratios, M15 autocorrelation, 4-hour variance ratio and realised vol separated good from bad periods only after the fact (|t| < 1.7). Optimising many such filters overfits to the in-sample regime, then the next trend year (2014-15, 2022) hits a ladder sized on filtered backtests.

failure_modes.mode: London-open breakout of the Asian range
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: After the first break of the Asian range in 07-11 UTC, price extends a further 9 pips (median), 26 pips (p90) and 56 pips (p99) within 60 minutes. A fade ladder opened at the range edge fills all layers one-way (inference, own computation).

failure_modes.mode: Stop-loss cascades through round numbers and fix-window volatility
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Stop orders cluster just beyond 00/50 levels, and crossing them speeds up the move for up to hours. The WMR 4pm fix and month-end produce extreme volatility. Ladders whose deep layers sit just past round levels, or that are open through fixes, fill several layers in one burst.

failure_modes.mode: Ladder depth × lots sized to typical moves, not the p99 30-minute excursion
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: 30-minute adverse excursions after a trigger reach 32-58 pips at p99 depending on session. At $0.10/pip per 0.01 lot, a 6-layer 0.01-step ladder (0.21 lots) loses about $70 on a 50-pip move, i.e. 70% of a $100 account. The hard time stop realises it instead of letting it recover (inference).

failure_modes.mode: Execution degradation on adds and exits (spread spikes between check and send, gap fills beyond deviation, last-look rejections, freeze-level modify rejections)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: The fills that matter most, adds during fast moves and basket exits, are where spread widens, LPs reject asymmetrically and modifies are frozen. Realised basket losses exceed what the model allowed.

failure_modes.mode: Rule or ToS breach (tick scalping, HFT, server spamming, position clustering)
failure_modes.why_accounts_blow: Sub-minute layer TPs, at least 3 opens within 60 s, and per-add TP modification of every position (thousands of requests per day) can trigger prop or broker abuse rules, leading to profit cancellation or account closure regardless of P&L.

Main results:
1. After a 1-sd 15-30 minute move, EURUSD's average snap-back is only +0.15 to +0.40 pip before costs. All-in cost is about 0.5-1.4 pip per round trip, so no regime filter can create a positive edge. Filters can only cut tail risk.
2. The ATR15/ATR1440 expansion ratio is the one feature that clearly separated fade-friendly from fade-hostile states. Efficiency ratio and a rolling variance ratio barely did, and Hurst is too noisy on short windows.
3. Sessions: the quiet Asian block after spreads normalise is the best place to grid. Avoid 19:00-23:00 UTC (rollover) and the London open around 07:00-08:30 UTC.
4. Size the ladder from the p99 30-minute adverse excursion (32-58 pips by session). On $100 that means about 3 layers and about 0.05-0.06 total lots.
5. Execution redesign: use a virtual basket TP instead of modifying every position after each add, enforce a 60-120 s cooldown between adds, and keep holds above 2 minutes on average.
6. Validate final candidates on the broker's real ticks with commission, Random delay and a CSV news calendar. MQL5's CalendarValueHistory returns nothing in the tester.
